text: Penicillin is able to inhibit bacterial growth without harming human cells because it targets what bacterial structure that animal cells lack?
explainAnswer: Identify the unique structures found in bacterial cells that are not present in human cells.
Recall that penicillin is an antibiotic that specifically interferes with bacterial cell functions.
Determine which structure in bacteria is essential for their survival and is targeted by penicillin.
Conclude that the structure targeted by penicillin is the cell wall, as animal cells do not have cell walls.

text: A father is colorblind, but his wife is not colorblind and is not a carrier of the gene for colorblindness. If the couple has a son, will he be colorblind?
choices: Yes, because colorblindness is always passed from father to son
No, because the mother is neither colorblind nor a carrier of colorblindness
There is a 50% chance because colorblindness is autosomal dominant
Yes, because the gene for colorblindness is located on the Y chromosome
explainAnswer: Identify that colorblindness is a sex-linked trait carried on the X chromosome.
Recognize that the father, being colorblind, has the genotype X^cY, where X^c represents the colorblind allele.
Understand that the mother, being neither colorblind nor a carrier, has the genotype XX.
Determine the possible genotypes of the son, which can only inherit the Y chromosome from the father and one X chromosome from the mother, resulting in XY.
Conclude that since the mother does not carry the colorblind allele, the son cannot be colorblind.

text: Which of the following organisms has a hydrostatic skeleton?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a hydrostatic skeleton, which is a structure found in some organisms that uses fluid pressure to maintain shape and support movement.
Evaluate each organism in the choices to determine if they possess a hydrostatic skeleton.
Humans have an endoskeleton, fish have a bony or cartilaginous skeleton, and lobsters have an exoskeleton.
Recognize that sea stars (echinoderms) use a water vascular system to create hydraulic pressure, which qualifies them as having a hydrostatic skeleton.
Conclude that the correct answer is sea star.

text: Which of the following leaf traits would be most useful in identifying the plants from which the leaves originated?
choices: Arrangement of leaves on the stem
explainAnswer: Consider the characteristics that are most distinctive for plant identification.
Evaluate each option based on how uniquely it can differentiate between plant species.
Determine that the arrangement of leaves on the stem is a key trait that varies significantly among different plants.
Conclude that while other traits may vary, leaf arrangement is a more reliable identifier.

text: Cellular respiration is used by the cell to produce what energetically relevant molecule?
explainAnswer: Identify the process of cellular respiration and its purpose in cells.
Recall that cellular respiration involves breaking down glucose and other molecules.
Recognize that the main product of this process is adenosine triphosphate (ATP).
Conclude that ATP is the energetically relevant molecule produced during cellular respiration.

text: A periwinkle is what type of organism?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of a periwinkle.
Research the classification of periwinkles in biological taxonomy.
Compare the characteristics of periwinkles with the given choices.
Determine which choice matches the classification of a periwinkle.

text: Which of the following is NOT true regarding B-vitamins:
choices: there are more than 5 different B-vitamins
vitamin B<sub>12</sub> is found in meat, milk and eggs
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of B-vitamins, noting that they are primarily water-soluble.
Review the list of B-vitamins to confirm that there are indeed more than 5, including B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B7, B9, and B12.
Verify that niacin is recognized as vitamin B3, confirming it is a B-vitamin.
Check the sources of vitamin B12, which are commonly found in animal products like meat, milk, and eggs.
Conclude that the statement 'they are fat soluble' is false, as B-vitamins are water-soluble.

text: What is the ultimate purpose of the Calvin cycle?
choices: To convert carbon dioxide into sugars
To convert waste products to oxygen
To convert sugars, fatty acids, and amino acids into ATP
To separate water into hydrogen and oxygen
explainAnswer: Identify the main processes involved in the Calvin cycle.
Recognize that the Calvin cycle is part of photosynthesis.
Understand that the Calvin cycle uses carbon dioxide as a key input.
Determine that the primary output of the Calvin cycle is sugars.

text: A new protein is discovered and scientists have deduced its chemical formula. To determine the 3-D shape of the protein, which of the following would be the appropriate step to take?
choices: Use computers to determine the 3-D shape based on its amino acid composition
Solidify it and use X-ray crystallography
Use a microscope to determine its tertiary and quaternary structures
Chemically break up the protein into smaller components to determine the overall structure
explainAnswer: Understand that X-ray crystallography is a technique used to determine the 3-D structure of proteins at atomic resolution.
Recognize that solidifying the protein into a crystal is a necessary step for X-ray crystallography.
Consider that other methods like computer modeling or microscopy may not provide the same level of detail as X-ray crystallography.
Conclude that solidifying the protein and using X-ray crystallography is the most appropriate method to accurately determine its 3-D shape.

text: Which of the following portions of the seed serves as the plant embryo's food supply until germination?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of each part of the seed mentioned in the choices.
Recall that the endosperm is known to provide nutrients to the developing embryo.
Eliminate the other options based on their functions: pollen is for reproduction, the embryo is the young plant, and the gametophyte is involved in the reproductive cycle.
Conclude that the endosperm is the correct answer as it serves as the food supply until germination.

text: Humans are part of what phylum [FYE- lum]?
explainAnswer: Identify the classification hierarchy in biology, starting from domain down to species.
Recognize that phylum is a major taxonomic rank in this hierarchy.
Recall that humans belong to the group characterized by having a notochord, which is a defining feature of the phylum Chordata.
Confirm that the correct term for the phylum is Chordata, not the plural form Chordates.

text: What is the scientific name for the white of a cooked egg?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of an egg, which include the shell, yolk, and white.
Recognize that the white of a cooked egg is commonly referred to as albumen.
Confirm that albumen is the scientific term for the egg white, distinguishing it from other parts of the egg.

text: Organize the following 3 tooth layers from the outermost to the innermost of a tooth: dentin, enamel, pulp
explainAnswer: Identify the three layers of a tooth: enamel, dentin, and pulp.
Determine the location of each layer in relation to the tooth structure.
Recognize that enamel is the outermost layer, followed by dentin, and pulp is the innermost layer.
Arrange the layers in order from outermost to innermost: enamel, dentin, pulp.

text: Place the following four items in order from smallest to largest: nucleus, ribosomes [RY-buh-sohms], mitochondria [my-tuh-KON-dree-uh], myoglobin [my-uh-GLOH-bin].
explainAnswer: Identify the size of each item: myoglobin is a small protein, ribosomes are larger than proteins but smaller than organelles, mitochondria are organelles, and the nucleus is the largest organelle.
Compare the sizes of myoglobin and ribosomes, noting that myoglobin is smaller.
Next, compare ribosomes and mitochondria, recognizing that ribosomes are smaller than mitochondria.
Then, compare mitochondria and the nucleus, concluding that the nucleus is larger than mitochondria.
Finally, arrange the items in order from smallest to largest: myoglobin, ribosomes, mitochondria, nucleus.

text: What is the net ATP gain of glycolysis?
explainAnswer: Recall that glycolysis is the process of breaking down glucose into pyruvate.
Identify that glycolysis produces a total of 4 ATP molecules through substrate-level phosphorylation.
Note that 2 ATP molecules are consumed in the initial steps of glycolysis.
Calculate the net gain by subtracting the consumed ATP from the produced ATP: 4 ATP produced - 2 ATP consumed = 2 ATP net gain.

text: In mammals, the Barr body is an inactivated form of which chromosome?
explainAnswer: Understand that Barr bodies are related to the process of X-inactivation in female mammals.
Recognize that females have two X chromosomes while males have one X and one Y chromosome.
Identify that one of the two X chromosomes in females is randomly inactivated to form a Barr body.
Conclude that the Barr body is an inactivated form of the X chromosome.

text: What small, regularly-shaped cell fragments circulate in the blood of mammals and lead to the formation of blood clots?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of blood and their functions.
Recall the role of cell fragments in the clotting process.
Determine which cell fragments are involved in hemostasis.
Conclude that the small, regularly-shaped cell fragments responsible for blood clots are platelets.

text: How many limbs are tetrapods typically considered to have?
explainAnswer: Identify what tetrapods are, which are vertebrates with four limbs.
Recall that the term 'tetrapod' comes from the Greek words for 'four' and 'foot'.
Recognize that tetrapods include animals such as amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals.
Conclude that tetrapods are typically considered to have 4 limbs.

text: What type of muscle is the intestine?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of muscle tissue in the human body: skeletal, cardiac, and smooth.
Recall that skeletal muscle is under voluntary control and is striated, while cardiac muscle is involuntary and striated.
Recognize that smooth muscle is involuntary and non-striated, found in the walls of hollow organs like the intestine.
Conclude that since the intestine is a hollow organ, it contains smooth muscle.

text: Which of the following populations of cells is likely to be most dramatically reduced in the brain of a patient with Parkinson's disease?
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics of Parkinson's disease, which primarily affects movement and motor control.
Understand that Parkinson's disease is associated with the degeneration of specific types of neurons in the brain.
Recognize that dopaminergic neurons are crucial for movement and are significantly impacted in Parkinson's disease.
Eliminate the other cell types listed (leukocytes, astroglia, motor neurons) as they are not primarily affected by Parkinson's disease.

text: What molecule is released from muscles as a waste product, transported to the lungs in blood, and exhaled as a gas?
explainAnswer: Identify the metabolic process in muscles that produces waste products.
Recognize that during cellular respiration, carbon dioxide is generated as a byproduct.
Understand that carbon dioxide is transported in the blood to the lungs.
Know that carbon dioxide is then exhaled from the lungs as a gas.

text: Identify all of the following four diseases that are caused by nematodes: 1) Chagas disease; 2) Toxoplasmosis; 3) Elephantiasis; 4) Heartworm disease.
explainAnswer: Understand that nematodes are a type of roundworm and identify diseases associated with them.
Research each disease to determine its causative agent.

Recognize that Chagas disease is caused by a protozoan, Toxoplasmosis is caused by a protozoan, Elephantiasis is caused by filarial nematodes, and Heartworm disease is caused by Dirofilaria immitis, a nematode.
Conclude that the diseases caused by nematodes from the list are Elephantiasis and Heartworm disease.

text: What organ in the human body is involved in filtering out extra solutes in the blood?
explainAnswer: Identify the organs involved in the circulatory and excretory systems.
Understand the primary functions of each organ related to blood filtration.
Recognize that the organ responsible for filtering out extra solutes is the kidney.
Confirm that the kidney plays a key role in maintaining homeostasis by regulating solute levels in the blood.

text: Chromosomes are composed of:
explainAnswer: Recall that chromosomes are structures within cells that carry genetic information.
Identify the components that make up chromosomes, focusing on their primary constituents.
Recognize that DNA is the molecule that holds genetic information, while proteins help in packaging and organizing this DNA.
Eliminate the other choices by confirming they do not accurately represent the composition of chromosomes.

text: Why are there no human vaccines against bacteriophages (read as: bahk-TIR-ee-oh-fay-jehs)?
answer: BACTERIOPHAGES DO NOT INFECT HUMANS (ACCEPT: BACTERIOPHAGES
explainAnswer: Identify what bacteriophages are and their role in infecting bacteria.
Understand that bacteriophages specifically target bacterial cells and do not infect human cells.
Recognize that vaccines are developed to protect against pathogens that infect humans.
Conclude that since bacteriophages do not infect humans, there is no need for human vaccines against them.

text: What are the common names of the two generally accepted families of living owls?
answer: TRUE (ACCEPT: TYPICAL) OWLS AND BARN OWLS
explainAnswer: Identify the general classification of owls in biology.
Research the two main families of living owls.
Recognize that one family is referred to as 'Typical Owls' and the other as 'Barn Owls'.
Confirm that these names are widely accepted in ornithology.

text: Conservation biology tries to preserve which of the following ecosystem characteristics?
choices: Large population size for all inhabiting species
Large population size for all inhabiting mammals
Elevated biodiversity for all forms of life
Elevated biodiversity for all macroscopic forms of life
explainAnswer: Identify the main goal of conservation biology, which is to protect ecosystems and their biodiversity.
Evaluate the choices given to determine which one aligns with the broad objectives of conservation biology.
Recognize that elevated biodiversity encompasses all forms of life, not just specific groups like mammals or macroscopic organisms.
Select the answer that reflects the comprehensive aim of conservation biology, which is to maintain elevated biodiversity for all forms of life.

text: By name or number, indicate all of the following three organisms that are examples of macrozooplankton: 1) cladocerans (read as: klah-DOH-seh- rahns), 2) rotifers, 3) adult copepods.
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of macrozooplankton and their size range.
Review the characteristics of each organism listed: cladocerans, rotifers, and adult copepods.
Determine which of the organisms meet the criteria for macrozooplankton based on size and classification.
Conclude that cladocerans and adult copepods are the correct examples, while rotifers do not qualify.

text: What is the most common term used to describe a hydrocarbon chain that has all single bonds between carbons?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of bonds present in the hydrocarbon chain.
Determine if the hydrocarbon contains only single bonds between carbon atoms.
Recall the terminology used to describe hydrocarbons based on their bonding.
Conclude that a hydrocarbon chain with all single bonds is referred to as saturated.

text: Identify all of the following four choices which are possible examples of fossils: 1) seeds, 2) footprints, 3) teeth, 4) cave drawings.
explainAnswer: Understand that fossils are the preserved remains or traces of ancient organisms.
Evaluate each option to determine if it represents a physical remnant or trace of a living organism from the past.
Recognize that seeds, footprints, and teeth can all be preserved as fossils, while cave drawings are not physical remains of organisms.

text: What is the most common name of the part of a neuron that takes its name from the Greek word for tree, and functions to carry electrical messages from other nerve cells to the soma?
explainAnswer: Identify the Greek word for tree, which is 'dendron'.
Recognize that the part of a neuron associated with receiving messages is called a dendrite.
Connect the Greek origin of the term to the function of the dendrite in the nervous system.
Conclude that the most common name for this part of the neuron is dendrite.

text: Given that hemophilia is a sex-linked trait, in a cross between a man with hemophilia and a female carrier, what percentage of their female offspring will be afflicted with hemophilia?
explainAnswer: Identify the genotypes of the parents: the man with hemophilia has the genotype X^hY and the female carrier has the genotype X^HX^h.
Set up a Punnett square to determine the possible genotypes of their offspring.
From the Punnett square, identify the female offspring genotypes: X^HX^h (carrier) and X^hX^h (affected).
Calculate the percentage of female offspring that will be afflicted with hemophilia by counting the affected genotypes.
Determine that 1 out of 2 female offspring (50%) will be afflicted with hemophilia.

text: The antibiotic penicillin halts bacterial growth by doing which of the following?
choices: Interfering with the synthesis of the bacterial cell wall
Interfering with the synthesis of bacterial ribosomes
Preventing attachment of messenger RNA to the ribosome
explainAnswer: Recall the mechanism of action of penicillin as an antibiotic.
Identify that penicillin specifically targets bacterial cell wall synthesis.
Eliminate other options that do not relate to cell wall synthesis.
Confirm that the correct choice is the one that mentions interference with the bacterial cell wall.

text: What plant was brought over from the Americas to Europe in the 1500’s and although was first thought to be poisonous soon became a staple because it had a high yield per acre and could be left un-harvested until needed.
explainAnswer: Identify the time period mentioned in the question, which is the 1500s.
Consider plants that were introduced to Europe from the Americas during that time.
Evaluate the characteristics of these plants, focusing on those that were initially thought to be poisonous.
Determine which of these plants became a staple due to high yield and storage capabilities.
Conclude that the plant in question is the potato.

text: Identify all of the following three disorders that are likely to be caused by non-disjunction events: 1) Down syndrome; 2) Tay-Sachs [saks]; 3) Turner syndrome.
explainAnswer: Understand that non-disjunction is the failure of chromosomes to separate properly during cell division.
Identify that Down syndrome is caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21 due to non-disjunction.
Recognize that Turner syndrome is caused by the absence of one X chromosome, also due to non-disjunction.
Note that Tay-Sachs is caused by a genetic mutation and not by non-disjunction, so it is not included.
Conclude that the disorders caused by non-disjunction are Down syndrome and Turner syndrome.

text: Sarcomeres [SAHR-koh-meers] compose the basic unit of what type of muscle?
explainAnswer: Recall that sarcomeres are the structural units of muscle tissue.
Identify the three types of muscle tissue: skeletal, cardiac, and smooth.
Determine which type of muscle tissue is composed of sarcomeres.
Conclude that sarcomeres are found in skeletal muscle.

text: By words or numbers, name all of the following that are organs in the human digestive system: 1) pancreas, 2) jejunum, 3) duodenum, and/or 4) bladder.
explainAnswer: Identify the organs involved in the human digestive system.
List the given options: pancreas, jejunum, duodenum, and bladder.
Determine which of these options are part of the digestive system.
Conclude that the pancreas, jejunum, and duodenum are correct, while the bladder is not.

text: What is the protein found in red blood cells that carries oxygen:
explainAnswer: Recall the primary function of red blood cells in the body.
Identify the molecule responsible for oxygen transport within these cells.
Remember that this molecule is a protein specifically designed for binding oxygen.
Conclude that the protein responsible for this function is hemoglobin.

text: A newborn baby was found to have 47 chromosomes. What is the term for this disorder?
explainAnswer: Identify that the normal number of chromosomes in humans is 46.
Recognize that having 47 chromosomes indicates an abnormal number.
Understand that an abnormal number of chromosomes is referred to as aneuploidy.
Eliminate the other options as they refer to specific types of chromosomal rearrangements rather than a change in number.

text: What organelle functions to isolate a human cell’s chromosomes from the cytoplasm?
explainAnswer: Identify the organelles within a human cell.
Determine which organelle is responsible for housing genetic material.
Consider the function of each organelle in relation to the cytoplasm.
Conclude that the organelle isolating chromosomes from the cytoplasm is the nucleus.

text: In ecology, what does the term detritus refer to?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which is ecology.
Review each choice to determine its relevance to ecological concepts.
Eliminate options that do not relate to organic material or decay.
Select the choice that accurately describes dead and decaying organic material.

text: What outer structure possessed by plant cells protects them from environmental changes and helps them maintain their shape during stress and times of water loss?
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics of plant cells that differentiate them from animal cells.
Recall the functions of various structures found in plant cells, such as the cell membrane, chloroplasts, and cell wall.
Focus on the structure that provides protection and maintains shape, especially during environmental stress.
Conclude that the structure responsible for these functions is the cell wall.

text: What process introduces genetic variation during meiosis [my-OH-sis] and does not occur during mitosis [my-TOW-sis] ?
explainAnswer: Understand the difference between meiosis and mitosis, focusing on their roles in cell division.
Identify the key stages of meiosis, particularly prophase I where genetic variation occurs.
Recognize that crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes during prophase I.
Conclude that crossing over is the process that introduces genetic variation and does not occur in mitosis.

text: Entomology is the study of what class of organisms?
explainAnswer: Identify the field of study mentioned in the question, which is entomology.
Recall that entomology is a branch of biology.
Associate entomology with its specific focus on a particular group of organisms.
Recognize that the specific group studied in entomology is insects.

text: Which of the following is the smallest object that a typical student compound light microscope is able to allow a person to see:
explainAnswer: Understand the typical magnification range of a compound light microscope, which is usually around 40x to 1000x.
Research the sizes of the objects in the choices: mRNA is about 2.5 nm, ribosomes are about 20 nm, E.coli bacteria are about 1-2 micrometers, and the polio virus is about 30 nm.
Compare the sizes of the objects to determine which one is large enough to be seen under the microscope's magnification.
Identify that E.coli, being a bacterium, is the largest among the given options and can be visualized under a compound light microscope.

text: What method for identifying protein structures involves the interpretation of diffraction patterns of proteins in the solid state?
answer: X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY (ACCEPT: X-RAY DIFFRACTION, DO NOT ACCEPT: X-
explainAnswer: Identify the methods used for determining protein structures.
Consider techniques that involve solid-state analysis.
Recall that diffraction patterns are a key component in these methods.
Recognize that X-ray crystallography specifically uses diffraction patterns to analyze protein structures.

text: A hospital technician centrifuges a vial of blood and notices a very thin milky white layer between two large layers. What can be found in these layers?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of blood: plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells (leukocytes), and platelets.
Understand that centrifugation separates blood into layers based on density.
Recognize that the top layer is plasma, the bottom layer is red blood cells, and the thin milky white layer in between contains leukocytes.
Conclude that the presence of a thin milky layer indicates the presence of leukocytes.

text: In which of the following parts of the kidney does filtration occur?
explainAnswer: Understand that the kidney has different parts with specific functions.
Identify that filtration is the process of removing waste and excess substances from blood.
Recognize that the renal corpuscle is the structure in the kidney where blood filtration occurs.
Eliminate the other options as they are involved in reabsorption or secretion, not filtration.

text: During prophase I, what process results in the exchange of DNA between homologous [ha-MAWL-uh-gus] chromosomes?
explainAnswer: Identify the stage of meiosis being discussed, which is prophase I.
Recall that during prophase I, homologous chromosomes pair up.
Understand that the exchange of DNA occurs between these paired homologous chromosomes.
Recognize that this exchange is specifically referred to as crossing over.

text: In a compound light microscope, what is the most common name of the lens closest to the specimen?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of a compound light microscope.
Recognize that there are multiple lenses in a microscope.
Determine which lens is positioned closest to the specimen.
Recall that this lens is primarily responsible for magnifying the specimen.
Conclude that the most common name for this lens is the objective lens.

text: What is the layer just below the canopy in the vertical stratification of a forest?
explainAnswer: Understand the concept of vertical stratification in a forest, which includes different layers such as the forest floor, understory, canopy, and emergent layer.
Identify the layer that is directly beneath the canopy, which is the uppermost layer of the forest.
Recognize that the layer below the canopy is where smaller trees and shrubs grow, which is referred to as the understory.
Confirm that the understory is characterized by lower light levels compared to the canopy, affecting the types of plants that can thrive there.

text: Alfred Wegener proposed what theory, which suggested that 200 million years ago, a supercontinent named Pangaea existed?
explainAnswer: Identify the key figure associated with the theory of continental movement.
Recall the name of the supercontinent proposed by this figure.
Connect the concept of the supercontinent to the theory that explains its formation and movement.
Conclude that the theory is known as continental drift.

text: Various parts of the human body show differences in relative growth rates. What principle explains this phenomenon?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of growth in different body parts during development.
Understand that allometric growth refers to the differential growth rates of various body parts.
Recognize that this principle explains how proportions change as an organism matures.
Relate allometric growth to the overall development and function of the organism.

text: The nutrient flow in an ecosystem can often be represented with a simple box model. What is the description for the ecosystem when the sources into and sinks out of the box are equal?
explainAnswer: Identify the terms 'sources' and 'sinks' in the context of an ecosystem.
Understand that 'sources' refer to inputs of nutrients and 'sinks' refer to outputs.
Recognize that when sources equal sinks, there is no net change in the amount of nutrients.
Conclude that this condition describes a system in balance, known as 'steady state'.

text: Which of the following is the most usable form of nitrogen for non-leguminous [non li-GYOO-muh-nuhs] plants?
explainAnswer: Identify the forms of nitrogen available for plants: ammonia, nitrogen gas, nitrites, and nitrates.
Understand that non-leguminous plants primarily absorb nitrogen in the form of nitrates.
Recall that nitrates are more readily taken up by plant roots compared to the other forms listed.
Conclude that among the options provided, nitrates are the most usable form of nitrogen for non-leguminous plants.

text: A brown mouse and a white mouse mate and have a litter of babies which are all brown. Assuming the trait is controlled by a simple dominant/recessive gene; use the appropriate scientific names to describe the genotypes for the coat color in each of the parents.
explainAnswer: Identify that the brown coat color is dominant and the white coat color is recessive.
Since all offspring are brown, the brown mouse must have at least one dominant allele.
Determine that the brown mouse must be homozygous dominant (BB) to ensure all offspring are brown.
Recognize that the white mouse must be homozygous recessive (bb) since it expresses the recessive trait.

text: Which of the following is the best reason that snakes do not reproduce with worms?
explainAnswer: Identify the reproductive barriers that can prevent species from interbreeding.
Evaluate the definitions of each type of isolation: temporal, habitat, behavioral, and mechanical.
Determine which type of isolation is related to physical differences that prevent mating.
Conclude that mechanical isolation is the best reason since snakes and worms have incompatible reproductive structures.

text: Given typical environmental abundances, which would you expect to be MOST abundant in a drop of seawater?
explainAnswer: Consider the typical sizes and populations of organisms in seawater.
Recall that viruses are much smaller than copepods, diatoms, and bacteria.
Understand that viruses can outnumber bacteria in marine environments by a significant margin.
Recognize that bacteria are abundant but still less numerous than viruses in seawater.
Conclude that, based on abundance, viruses are expected to be the most abundant in a drop of seawater.

text: What disaccharide sugar is formed from galactose and glucose?
explainAnswer: Identify the two monosaccharides involved: galactose and glucose.
Recall that disaccharides are formed by the condensation of two monosaccharides.
Determine the specific disaccharide formed from the combination of galactose and glucose.
Conclude that the disaccharide formed is lactose.

text: When bees pollinate a flower for nectar, both of the species benefit from this interaction. What is the specific term for this type of symbiosis?
explainAnswer: Identify the relationship between the two species involved in the interaction.
Determine if both species benefit from the interaction.
Recall the specific terms used to describe different types of symbiotic relationships.
Conclude that the term for a relationship where both species benefit is mutualism.

text: Honeybees and other pollinators transfer pollen from the:
choices: Anther to the Stigma of the Flower
Stigma to the Anther of the Flower
Filament to the Sepal of the Flower
Sepal to the Filament of the Flower
explainAnswer: Identify the parts of a flower involved in pollination: anther, stigma, filament, and sepal.
Understand that the anther produces pollen and the stigma is where pollen lands for fertilization.
Recognize that pollinators, like honeybees, transfer pollen from the anther to the stigma.
Eliminate the other choices based on the roles of the flower parts in reproduction.

text: Which of the following pairs is NOT a correct matching of an organism with its external symmetry classification?
explainAnswer: Identify the symmetry classification of each organism listed in the choices.
Heliozoans are spherical, crocodiles are bilateral, and starfish are radial.
Determine the correct symmetry for lobsters, which are actually bilateral.
Compare the classifications to find the pair that does not match.

text: What is the common name of the type of blood cells found in elevated numbers in a person who has an infection?
explainAnswer: Recall the types of blood cells in the human body.
Identify which blood cells are primarily involved in the immune response.
Consider the role of these cells during an infection.
Conclude that the type of blood cells that increase in number during an infection are white blood cells.

text: Your neighbor just cut down a tree that he claims germinated the year he was born. What do you need to count to determine the plausibility of your neighbor's story?
explainAnswer: Identify that trees grow by adding layers of xylem each year.
Understand that xylem rings represent the annual growth of the tree.
Count the number of xylem rings to determine the age of the tree.
Compare the age of the tree to your neighbor's birth year to assess the plausibility of his claim.

text: What is the term for a heritable change in the character of a gene or a change in the sequence of base pairs in a DNA molecule?
explainAnswer: Identify the key concepts related to genetics and heredity.
Recall the definitions of terms associated with genetic changes.
Determine which term specifically refers to changes in DNA sequences.
Conclude that the term for a heritable change in a gene is 'mutation'.

text: Name the three main protein filaments that make up the cytoskeleton.
explainAnswer: Recall the components of the cytoskeleton in eukaryotic cells.
Identify the three types of protein filaments associated with the cytoskeleton.
List the filaments as microfilaments, intermediate filaments, and microtubules.

text: What is the term for cells that contain membrane-bound nuclei?
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics of different types of cells.
Recall that eukaryotic cells are defined by having a membrane-bound nucleus.
Differentiate between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells based on their structural features.
Conclude that the term for cells with membrane-bound nuclei is eukaryotes.

text: Name the three subdivisions of the small intestine.
explainAnswer: Recall the anatomy of the digestive system, focusing on the small intestine.
Identify the three main sections of the small intestine.
List the sections as DUODENUM, JEJUNUM, and ILEUM.

text: In aerobic respiration, what is the terminal electron acceptor in the electron transport chain?
explainAnswer: Recall the process of aerobic respiration and its stages.
Identify the role of the electron transport chain in cellular respiration.
Determine which molecule acts as the final acceptor of electrons in this chain.
Conclude that oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor.

text: Which of the following plants traps and digests insects:
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of each plant listed in the choices.
Research which of the plants are known for insect trapping and digestion.
Confirm that sun dew is a type of carnivorous plant that traps insects.
Eliminate the other options based on their known characteristics and functions.

text: To which of the following virus classes does HIV belong?
explainAnswer: Recall the characteristics of the listed virus classes.
Identify that HIV is known for its ability to reverse transcribe RNA into DNA.
Match this characteristic with the definition of a retrovirus.
Eliminate the other options based on their definitions and characteristics.

text: Which of the following organisms contains the most chitin (read as: KYE-tin) by percent of body weight:
explainAnswer: Identify the organisms listed in the choices and their general characteristics.
Understand that chitin is a structural polysaccharide commonly found in the exoskeletons of arthropods.
Recognize that among the given options, the ant is an arthropod and has a significant percentage of its body weight composed of chitin.
Compare the body compositions of the other organisms, noting that they do not have chitin as a major component.
Conclude that the ant contains the most chitin by percent of body weight compared to the other organisms.

text: Inflammation can be driven by what signaling molecule that is contained within mast cells, and whose inhibitors are commonly used as allergy medications?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of mast cells in the immune response.
Recall the signaling molecules stored in mast cells that are involved in inflammation.
Determine which of these molecules is commonly associated with allergic reactions.
Recognize that the inhibitors of this molecule are used in allergy medications.

text: The glycemic index is an index that is used to directly predict the rate at which ingested food in the human diet will increase which of the following levels in the blood:
explainAnswer: Identify what the glycemic index measures in relation to food consumption.
Consider the physiological effects of different types of food on the body.
Eliminate options that do not relate to food intake and blood levels.
Confirm that the glycemic index specifically relates to blood sugar levels.

text: What scientist is credited with showing that all cells come from preexisting cells?
explainAnswer: Identify the key concept that all cells originate from preexisting cells.
Recall the contributions of each scientist listed in the choices.
Recognize that Rudolf Virchow is known for formulating the principle of biogenesis.
Eliminate the other options based on their contributions to cell theory.
Confirm that Rudolf Virchow is the correct answer.

text: Which of the following is true?
choices: Meiosis [my-OH-sis] results in two daughter cells
Meiosis results in identical daughter cells
Mitosis [my-TOH-sis] results in four daughter cells
Mitosis results in identical daughter cells
explainAnswer: Identify the key processes being compared: meiosis and mitosis.
Recall that meiosis results in four non-identical daughter cells, while mitosis results in two identical daughter cells.
Evaluate each choice based on the definitions and outcomes of meiosis and mitosis.
Determine that the only true statement is that mitosis results in identical daughter cells.

text: If the widest point on a population pyramid is located at the middle-age range then population growth is:
explainAnswer: Identify that a population pyramid shows the distribution of various age groups in a population.
Recognize that a wider base indicates a larger number of younger individuals, while a wider middle suggests a stable or declining birth rate.
Understand that if the widest point is in the middle-age range, it implies fewer young people are entering the population.
Conclude that this situation typically leads to a negative population growth trend.

text: How many chromatids would you find in a tetrad?
explainAnswer: Understand that a tetrad is formed during meiosis when homologous chromosomes pair up.
Recognize that each homologous chromosome consists of two sister chromatids.
Calculate the total number of chromatids by multiplying the number of homologous chromosomes (2) by the number of chromatids per chromosome (2).
Thus, 2 homologous chromosomes x 2 chromatids each = 4 chromatids in total.

text: Which of the following coordinate cell division?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of each cell component listed in the choices.
Recall that centrioles are involved in organizing microtubules during cell division.
Eliminate options that do not play a direct role in coordinating cell division.
Confirm that centrioles are essential for the formation of the spindle apparatus during mitosis.

text: Identify all of the following three diseases that are caused by fungi: 1) Yeast infection; 2) Tuberculosis; 3) Ringworm.
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of each disease listed.
Determine which of the diseases are caused by fungal pathogens.
Confirm that a yeast infection is caused by fungi (Candida species).
Confirm that ringworm is caused by fungi (dermatophytes).
Recognize that tuberculosis is caused by bacteria, not fungi.

text: Which of the following is NOT found in an animal cell?
explainAnswer: Identify the components listed in the choices.
Recall the structure and function of each component in relation to animal cells.
Recognize that a cell wall is characteristic of plant cells and not animal cells.
Conclude that the correct answer is the component that is not found in animal cells.

text: Identify all of the following five choices that may serve as food for a hornet: 1) house fly, 2) blow fly, 3) pollen, 4) caterpillar, 5) tree sap.
answer: 1, 2, 4, 5 (HOUSE FLY, BLOW FLY, CATERPILLAR, TREE SAP)
explainAnswer: Understand that hornets are carnivorous and primarily feed on other insects.
Identify which of the choices are insects or insect-related food sources.
Recognize that house flies and blow flies are both types of insects that hornets can prey on.
Note that caterpillars are also insects and can be consumed by hornets.
Acknowledge that tree sap can be a food source for hornets, while pollen is not typically consumed by them.

text: What male reproductive part of a plant produces pollen?
explainAnswer: Identify the male reproductive structures of a plant, which include the stamen.
Recognize that the stamen consists of two parts: the filament and the anther.
Recall that the anther is the part of the stamen that produces and contains pollen.
Conclude that the correct answer is the anther.

text: Aside from neurons, what other general type of cells are found in the nervous system?
explainAnswer: Recall the main components of the nervous system.
Identify the two primary types of cells in the nervous system: neurons and glial cells.
Recognize that glial cells support and protect neurons.
Conclude that glial cells are the other general type of cells found in the nervous system.

text: Which of the following locations in a chloroplast has the highest acidity?
explainAnswer: Understand that acidity is related to the concentration of hydrogen ions (H+) in a solution.
Recognize that during photosynthesis, protons are pumped into the thylakoid lumen, increasing its H+ concentration.
Compare the environments of the granum, stroma, and intermembrane space to the thylakoid lumen regarding H+ concentration.
Conclude that the thylakoid lumen has the highest acidity due to the accumulation of protons during the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.

text: A plant cell contains two external layers. One layer gives support to the cell but does not filter what may enter and exit. The other layer does not provide support but does filter compounds. Respectively, name the two layers.
explainAnswer: Identify the two external layers of a plant cell.
Determine which layer provides structural support without filtering substances.
Identify the layer that filters compounds but does not provide support.
Conclude that the supportive layer is the cell wall and the filtering layer is the plasma membrane.

text: What iron cofactor is found in the human respiratory pigment in blood?
explainAnswer: Identify the main function of the human respiratory pigment in blood, which is hemoglobin.
Recognize that hemoglobin contains an iron-containing component essential for oxygen transport.
Recall that the specific iron cofactor associated with hemoglobin is heme, not just iron (Fe).
Conclude that the correct answer is heme, as it is the functional group that binds oxygen.

text: A student puts an elodea plant into a test tube and adds water and baking soda. After putting the test tube under 24 hours of light, the student notices bubbles forming on the leaves. The bubbles are most probably which of the following?
explainAnswer: Identify that the elodea plant is undergoing photosynthesis in the presence of light.
Recognize that photosynthesis produces oxygen as a byproduct when plants convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.
Note that the bubbles forming on the leaves are likely to be the oxygen produced during this process.
Eliminate the other gas options since they do not result from the photosynthesis process in this context.

text: Vestigial (pronounced VES-ti-gee-al) structures:
choices: have no known function in their present owners
function in an analogous fashion in all species
explainAnswer: Understand the definition of vestigial structures, which are remnants of organs or structures that had a function in early ancestors.
Evaluate each choice to see if it aligns with the definition of vestigial structures.
Identify that the correct choice states that vestigial structures have no known function in their present owners.
Eliminate the other choices based on their descriptions not fitting the definition of vestigial structures.

text: What artery originates in the left ventricle of the heart and extends down to the abdomen?
explainAnswer: Identify the major arteries that originate from the heart.
Recall that the left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta.
Understand that the aorta is the largest artery in the body.
Recognize that the aorta extends down to the abdomen, supplying blood to the lower body.

text: By name or number, identify all of the following which can represent either sexual or asexual reproduction: 1) plant seed generation, 2) bacteria binary fission, 3) fungi sporulation, and/or 4) yeast budding.
answer: PLANT SEED GENERATION AND FUNGI SPORULATION
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of sexual and asexual reproduction.
Determine if each option represents sexual reproduction, asexual reproduction, or both.
Plant seed generation involves the fusion of gametes, indicating sexual reproduction.
Fungi sporulation can involve both sexual and asexual processes depending on the species.
Bacteria binary fission and yeast budding are examples of asexual reproduction only.

text: The tracheal system in insects includes many small external openings on the sides of their bodies. What function does this system serve?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of the tracheal system in insects.
Consider the role of small external openings in relation to gas exchange.
Eliminate options that do not relate to the exchange of gases.
Conclude that the primary function of the tracheal system is respiration.

text: In birds, which of the following is the correct order of organs in digestion?
explainAnswer: Understand the basic digestive system of birds, which includes the crop, stomach, gizzard, and intestine.
Identify the function of each organ: the crop stores food, the stomach begins digestion, the gizzard grinds food, and the intestine absorbs nutrients.
Determine the correct sequence of these organs based on their roles in the digestion process.
Select the option that lists the organs in the identified correct order: Crop, Stomach, Gizzard, Intestine.

text: The role of cristae is to increase the surface area of the inner membrane of what eukaryotic organelle?
explainAnswer: Identify the organelle involved in energy production in eukaryotic cells.
Recall that the inner membrane of this organelle has folds called cristae.
Understand that the purpose of cristae is to increase the surface area for chemical reactions.
Conclude that the organelle in question is the mitochondria.

text: Order the following 5 digestive system parts, from the part of the digestive tract nearest to the beginning to the part nearest to the end: esophagus, ileum, duodenum, jejunum, uvula
explainAnswer: Identify the parts of the digestive system listed: uvula, esophagus, duodenum, jejunum, ileum.
Determine the location of each part in the digestive tract, starting from the mouth and ending at the intestines.
Place the uvula at the beginning as it is located in the mouth.
Next, place the esophagus as it connects the throat to the stomach.
Then, order the small intestine parts: duodenum, jejunum, and ileum, from the beginning to the end.

text: In the earthworm digestive system, what is the term for the pouch in which mechanical digestion of food occurs?
explainAnswer: Recall the main parts of the earthworm's digestive system.
Identify the function of each part, focusing on where mechanical digestion occurs.
Recognize that the pouch responsible for mechanical digestion is called the gizzard.
Confirm that the gizzard is located after the crop and before the intestine.

text: Which of the following is the most common source of energy for brain cells in humans:
explainAnswer: Identify the primary functions of the brain and its energy requirements.
Consider the different macromolecules listed in the choices and their roles in energy metabolism.
Recall that glucose is a key energy source for cellular respiration in brain cells.
Eliminate the other options based on their relevance to energy production in the brain.

text: Which of the following membrane transport methods is most important for release of neurotransmitters like acetylcholine during synaptic signaling?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of neurotransmitters in synaptic signaling.
Understand that neurotransmitters are released from neurons into the synaptic cleft.
Recognize that exocytosis is the process by which vesicles fuse with the membrane to release contents.
Eliminate other transport methods that do not involve the release of substances from vesicles.

text: Order the following 4 parts of the human intestine from the FIRST to receive food from the stomach to the LAST: colon; duodenum; ileum; jejunum
explainAnswer: Identify the sequence of the human intestine parts involved in digestion.
Recognize that the duodenum is the first part to receive food from the stomach.
Follow with the jejunum, which is the second part of the small intestine.
Next is the ileum, which is the final part of the small intestine.
Conclude with the colon, which is part of the large intestine.

text: Which of the following is NOT a source of food for polar bears in the wild?
explainAnswer: Identify the natural habitat of polar bears, which is the Arctic region.
List the common prey of polar bears found in their habitat, such as seals and whales.
Recognize that emperor penguins are native to Antarctica, not the Arctic.
Determine which option does not belong to the polar bear's food sources based on their geographical distribution.

text: Which of the following structures can be found in an E. coli cell?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of E. coli as a prokaryotic organism.
Recall that prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles such as a nucleus and mitochondria.
Recognize that ribosomes are present in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells for protein synthesis.
Eliminate the choices that cannot be found in E. coli based on its prokaryotic nature.
Conclude that ribosomes are the only structures listed that can be found in an E. coli cell.

text: Of the 4 general types of biological molecules, proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids, which one will typically release the MOST energy per gram when metabolized by a normal healthy human?
explainAnswer: Identify the four general types of biological molecules: proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, and nucleic acids.
Understand that energy release during metabolism is related to the molecular structure and composition of these molecules.
Recall that lipids have a higher caloric density due to their long hydrocarbon chains, which provide more energy when oxidized.
Compare the energy yield per gram of each type of molecule, noting that lipids typically yield more energy than proteins and carbohydrates.

text: Which of the following DNA mutations is most likely to occur?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of mutations listed in the choices.
Recognize that DNA uses the bases A, T, C, and G, while RNA uses U instead of T.
Determine which mutations involve only the bases found in DNA.
Evaluate the likelihood of each mutation occurring based on base pairing and common mutations.
Conclude that A to G is a common transition mutation that can occur in DNA.

text: Which of the following environmental limits on population growth is density-independent?
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of density-dependent and density-independent factors.
Recall that density-dependent factors are influenced by population density, while density-independent factors affect populations regardless of their size.
Evaluate each option: Disease, Parasites, and Competition are all influenced by population density.
Recognize that Weather affects populations regardless of their density, making it density-independent.
Conclude that Weather is the correct answer.

text: Name all of the following 4 cellular structures that are found in plant cells and NOT bacteria: mitochondria; chloroplasts; cell membranes; ribosomes
explainAnswer: Identify the cellular structures listed in the question.
Determine which of these structures are present in plant cells.
Check if each structure is also found in bacteria.
List the structures that are found in plant cells but not in bacteria.

text: An intracellular substance is so named because it is located in which of the following places:
explainAnswer: Identify the meaning of the term 'intracellular', which refers to something located inside a cell.
Eliminate options that do not align with the definition of 'intracellular'.
Recognize that 'within cells' is the only choice that accurately describes the location of intracellular substances.
Select 'within cells' as the correct answer.

text: Which of the following is the scientific name for the thigh bone:
explainAnswer: Identify the common names of the bones listed in the choices.
Recall that the thigh bone is the largest bone in the human body.
Match the common name 'thigh bone' with its scientific name from the choices given.
Select 'femur' as it is known scientifically as the thigh bone.

text: A potato is a swollen underground stem that stores food for the plant. What is the scientific term for the swollen area?
explainAnswer: Identify the part of the plant being described, which is the underground stem.
Understand the function of this part, which is to store food.
Recall the scientific terminology associated with swollen underground stems.
Conclude that the correct term for this swollen area is 'tuber'.

text: Which of the following are NOT bryophytes (read as: BRY- oh-fyts):?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of bryophytes, which are non-vascular plants that include liverworts, hornworts, and mosses.
Review the list of choices to determine which plants are classified as bryophytes.
Recognize that ferns are vascular plants and do not fall under the category of bryophytes.
Conclude that ferns are the correct answer as they are NOT bryophytes.

text: What is the final electron acceptor in the Krebs cycle before the electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation [FOS-fohr-uh-lay-shuhn]?
explainAnswer: Understand that the Krebs cycle, also known as the citric acid cycle, is part of cellular respiration.
Identify that during the Krebs cycle, electrons are transferred to electron carriers.
Recognize that the main electron carriers produced in the Krebs cycle are NADH and FADH2.
Know that NAD+ is the oxidized form of NADH and acts as the final electron acceptor in the Krebs cycle.
Conclude that NAD+ is necessary for the continuation of the cycle and for feeding electrons into the electron transport chain.

text: Which of the following biological molecules make up the main part of the bilayer and hydrophobic region of the plasma cell membrane:
explainAnswer: Identify the components of the plasma cell membrane, which include various types of biological molecules.
Understand that the plasma membrane is primarily composed of a lipid bilayer.
Recognize that phospholipids are the main type of lipids that form this bilayer due to their hydrophilic heads and hydrophobic tails.
Eliminate the other options (oligosaccharides, carbohydrates, proteins) as they do not primarily form the bilayer structure.

text: What is the term for a region of DNA that encodes all of the information for a specific protein?
explainAnswer: Identify the basic unit of heredity in living organisms.
Recall that this unit is responsible for encoding proteins.
Consider the definition of a segment of DNA that carries this information.
Conclude that the term for this segment is 'gene'.

text: Villi and microvilli in the small intestine, cristae in the mitochondrial inner membrane, and thylakoids in the plant chloroplast are structures that evolved to maximize what physical property?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of villi, microvilli, cristae, and thylakoids in their respective organelles.
Recognize that these structures are adaptations that increase the efficiency of their functions.
Understand that increasing the surface area allows for more reactions or processes to occur simultaneously.
Conclude that the common physical property maximized by these structures is surface area.

text: Marsupials are far more abundant and diverse in Australia than in North and South America. Which of the following best explains why only three families of marsupials are found outside the Australian region?
explainAnswer: Identify the key concept of marsupials and their distribution across continents.
Understand the definitions of the types of evolution: divergent, convergent, parallel, and antiparallel.
Recognize that divergent evolution explains how species evolve differently from a common ancestor when they are separated by geographical barriers.
Apply this understanding to the fact that marsupials evolved in isolation in Australia, leading to greater diversity there compared to the limited families found elsewhere.
Conclude that the best explanation for the limited presence of marsupials outside Australia is divergent evolution.

text: What is the name of a method of fertilization in which the ovum is fertilized within a fallopian tube of a fertile female donor for transplantation into an infertile recipient?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question, such as 'fertilization', 'ovum', and 'fallopian tube'.
Understand the context of fertilization methods, distinguishing between in vivo and in vitro techniques.
Recognize that the process described involves fertilization occurring inside a living organism rather than in a lab.
Conclude that the term for this method is 'in vivo fertilization' based on the definition provided.

text: Which of the following groups are all invertebrates?
choices: Snails, honeybees, sea star, and sea sponges
Grasshoppers, fruit flies, electric eels, and sea horses
explainAnswer: Identify which groups consist of only invertebrates, which are animals without a backbone.
Review each choice and categorize the animals listed as either invertebrates or vertebrates.
Eliminate any groups that contain vertebrates, such as bats, fish, electric eels, cows, pigs, horses, and chickens.
Confirm that the remaining group, which includes snails, honeybees, sea stars, and sea sponges, consists entirely of invertebrates.

text: Which of the following is NOT true about the black-footed ferret?
choices: They like to eat prairie dogs
They neared total extinction in the 1980s
They like to live in groups
They have one to six young in a litter
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of the black-footed ferret from reliable sources.
Review each statement provided in the choices to determine their accuracy.
Cross-reference the statement about living in groups with known behavior of black-footed ferrets.
Determine which statement is false based on the gathered information.

text: Some bacteriophages [bak-TEER-ee-oh-fay-jez] do not immediately kill the bacteria that they infect; rather, they incorporate themselves into the host genome [JEE-nome] . What is the term for the incorporated virus?
explainAnswer: Identify the key concept of bacteriophages and their interaction with host bacteria.
Understand the difference between lytic and lysogenic cycles of bacteriophages.
Recognize that a virus incorporated into the host genome is referred to as a prophage.
Eliminate the other options based on their definitions and roles in the bacteriophage life cycle.
Select 'Prophage' as the correct answer.

text: Which of the following kinds of microscopes typically is used to view the surface of objects ranging in size from cells to small insects like fleas to reveal minute surface details:
explainAnswer: Identify the types of microscopes listed in the choices.
Understand the primary function of each type of microscope.
Recognize that scanning electron microscopy is specifically designed to view surface details at a high resolution.
Eliminate the other options based on their typical applications and capabilities.
Conclude that scanning electron microscopy is the correct choice for viewing minute surface details of small objects.

text: Photosynthesis has both light and dark reactions. Which of the following occurs WITHOUT the presence of light?
choices: Water is split to produce oxygen
Carbon dioxide is transformed to sugar
explainAnswer: Identify the processes involved in photosynthesis, distinguishing between light-dependent and light-independent reactions.
Recall that the light-dependent reactions require light to occur, while the light-independent reactions (Calvin cycle) do not.
Recognize that the transformation of carbon dioxide into sugar occurs during the light-independent reactions.
Eliminate the other options that involve light-dependent processes, such as water splitting and ATP production.

text: What process do autotrophs use to make their own food from sunlight?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of autotrophs as organisms that produce their own food.
Recall the role of sunlight in the food production process for these organisms.
Understand that the specific process used by autotrophs to convert sunlight into food is known as photosynthesis.
Recognize that photosynthesis involves converting carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen using sunlight.

text: What is the name for the muscle that contracts when you inhale and causes your chest cavity to expand?
explainAnswer: Identify the muscle involved in the process of inhalation.
Recall the function of the diaphragm in respiratory mechanics.
Confirm that the diaphragm is the primary muscle that contracts to expand the chest cavity during inhalation.
Conclude that the name of this muscle is diaphragm.

text: Coal formed from the remains of plants that died more than 300 million years ago. In what period did these plants live?
explainAnswer: Identify the time frame mentioned in the question, which is more than 300 million years ago.
Recall the geological time periods and their approximate dates.
Recognize that the Carboniferous period occurred approximately 359 to 299 million years ago.
Eliminate the other periods based on their timelines: Precambrian is much older, Cenozoic is much younger, and Cretaceous is also younger.
Conclude that the plants that formed coal lived during the Carboniferous period.

text: Which of the following does NOT contribute to eutrophication [yoo-tro-fi-KAY-shun]?
explainAnswer: Identify the process of eutrophication and its causes.
Recognize that eutrophication is primarily driven by nutrient overload, particularly nitrogen and phosphorus.
Evaluate each option to see if it contributes nutrients to water bodies.
Determine that increased oxygen inputs do not add nutrients and therefore do not contribute to eutrophication.

text: Hydrogen peroxide is often used to clean wounds. It reacts with catalase to do which of the following?
choices: Generate toxins that stop bacterial cell wall production
explainAnswer: Identify that hydrogen peroxide is a substrate for the enzyme catalase.
Recall that catalase catalyzes the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide.
Recognize that this reaction produces water and oxygen as products.
Conclude that the correct answer is 'Generate pure oxygen' based on the reaction outcome.

text: Which two valves are located between the atria and ventricles of the heart?
explainAnswer: Identify the main chambers of the heart: the atria and ventricles.
Recognize that the valves between the atria and ventricles are responsible for controlling blood flow.
Recall the names of the valves: the mitral valve is between the left atrium and left ventricle, and the tricuspid valve is between the right atrium and right ventricle.
Eliminate the incorrect choices based on the locations of the valves.

text: What group of fungi reproduces only by asexual means or has a sexual cycle that has not yet been observed?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of fungi that reproduce asexually.
Research the classification of fungi and look for groups that lack a known sexual reproduction cycle.
Confirm that the group known as Fungi Imperfecti fits these criteria.
Conclude that Fungi Imperfecti is the correct answer based on the definitions and classifications found.

text: Identify all of the following three choices that arise, directly or indirectly, from meristematic activity: 1) Leaves; 2) Dermal tissue; 3) Xylem.
explainAnswer: Understand that meristematic tissue is responsible for the growth of plants and gives rise to various plant structures.
Identify that leaves develop from the apical meristem, which is a type of meristematic tissue.
Recognize that dermal tissue originates from the protoderm, which is also derived from meristematic activity.
Note that xylem is produced from the procambium, another meristematic tissue responsible for vascular development.
Conclude that all three choices (leaves, dermal tissue, and xylem) arise from meristematic activity.

text: Which of the following artificial sweeteners must be avoided by people who suffer from phenylketonuria [fen-l -kee-toh-NOOR-ee-uh]?
explainAnswer: Identify the condition: phenylketonuria (PKU) is a metabolic disorder that affects the body's ability to process phenylalanine.
Recognize that aspartame is a sweetener that contains phenylalanine, which is harmful to individuals with PKU.
Review the other sweeteners listed to confirm they do not contain phenylalanine.
Conclude that aspartame must be avoided by people with phenylketonuria.

text: Hemophilia is an X-chromosome-linked recessive trait. Which of the following percentages is the probability that the daughter of a male with the disease and a female carrier is a hemophiliac?
explainAnswer: Identify the genotypes of the parents: the male with hemophilia has genotype X^hY, and the female carrier has genotype X^HX^h.
Determine the possible gametes from each parent: the male can contribute X^h or Y, and the female can contribute X^H or X^h.
Create a Punnett square to visualize the combinations of the gametes: the combinations will be X^HX^h, X^hX^h, X^HY, and X^hY.
Analyze the offspring: the daughter can be X^HX^h (carrier) or X^hX^h (hemophiliac), leading to a 50% chance of being a hemophiliac.
Conclude that the probability that the daughter is a hemophiliac is 50%.

text: Tapeworms can infect the human digestive tract, where they grow and persist for long periods of time, causing relatively moderate symptoms such as diarrhea and anemia. Therefore, tapeworms are best described as which of the following?
explainAnswer: Identify the relationship between the tapeworm and the human host.
Determine if the tapeworm benefits at the expense of the host's health.
Evaluate the definitions of commensalists, mutualists, and parasitoids to see which does not fit.
Conclude that since the tapeworm harms the host while benefiting itself, it is best described as a parasite.

text: What force allows the xylem to transport water against gravity?
explainAnswer: Understand that xylem is responsible for transporting water in plants.
Recognize that capillary action is the ability of liquid to flow in narrow spaces without the assistance of external forces.
Identify that capillary action occurs due to the cohesive and adhesive properties of water.
Conclude that capillary action enables water to move upward against gravity in the xylem.

text: In 1986, Lynn Margulis proposed the endosymbiont theory. Which of the following is NOT evidence for this recent theory?
choices: Mitochondria and chloroplasts reproduce by fission
Mitochondria and chloroplasts contain their own DNA, which is arranged in a circular pattern as found in prokaryotes
Mitochondria and chloroplasts contain peptidoglycan in their outer membranes like some prokaryotes
Mitochondria and chloroplasts contain ribosomes that resemble ribosomes in prokaryotes
explainAnswer: Identify the key components of the endosymbiont theory proposed by Lynn Margulis.
Review the evidence supporting the theory, focusing on the characteristics of mitochondria and chloroplasts.
Evaluate each choice to determine if it aligns with the known evidence for the endosymbiont theory.
Recognize that peptidoglycan is not found in mitochondria and chloroplasts, making that statement the correct answer.
Select the option that does not provide valid evidence for the endosymbiont theory.

text: To what phylum [FYE- lum] does baker's yeast belong?
explainAnswer: Identify that baker's yeast is a type of fungus.
Recall the classification of fungi into different phyla.
Determine that baker's yeast is specifically known as Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
Recognize that Saccharomyces cerevisiae belongs to the phylum Ascomycota.
Select Ascomycota as the correct answer.

text: Which of the following trees have simple, pinnate leaves:
explainAnswer: Identify the leaf structure of each tree in the choices provided.
Determine which trees have simple leaves, meaning each leaf is a single blade.
Check if the identified simple leaves are pinnate, where leaflets are arranged on either side of a central vein.
Compare the findings to the choices and select the pair that meets both criteria of being simple and pinnate.

text: Which of the following is NOT true about nicotine:
choices: chewing or smokeless tobaccos are safe when used properly because nicotine cannot be absorbed through the mucous membrane
nicotine and cyanide have been found in cigarettes
during pregnancy, nicotine concentrates in breast milk and fetal blood
nicotine is a plant alkaloid that is poisonous to most animals
explainAnswer: Identify the statements provided in the choices.
Evaluate each statement for its truthfulness based on scientific knowledge about nicotine.
Recognize that nicotine can indeed be absorbed through the mucous membranes.
Determine which statement is false based on your evaluation.
Conclude that the incorrect statement is about the safety of chewing or smokeless tobaccos.

text: When immersed in a hypertonic solution, a plant cell membrane will pull away from the cell wall. What is the name of this phenomenon?
explainAnswer: Identify the condition of the plant cell when placed in a hypertonic solution.
Understand that a hypertonic solution causes water to leave the cell.
Recognize that the loss of water leads to the cell membrane shrinking away from the cell wall.
Recall the term used to describe this specific process of the cell membrane pulling away from the cell wall.

text: What cells are composed of a cell body, dendrites, and axons?
explainAnswer: Identify the components mentioned: cell body, dendrites, and axons.
Recall the function of these components in relation to signaling.
Recognize that these components are specific to a certain type of cell in the nervous system.
Conclude that the cells being described are neurons.

text: Synaptic vesicles contain what signaling molecules?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of synaptic vesicles in the nervous system.
Recall that synaptic vesicles are responsible for storing and releasing signaling molecules.
Recognize that the primary type of signaling molecules released by synaptic vesicles are neurotransmitters.
Conclude that neurotransmitters are the correct answer to what synaptic vesicles contain.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true regarding sugars: 1) Glucose, fructose, and galactose are structural isomers; 2) Glucose, fructose, and galactose are hexose sugars; 3) Lactose is a disaccharide [dye-SAK-ah-ride] composed of glucose and galactose.
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of structural isomers and check if glucose, fructose, and galactose have the same molecular formula but different structures.
Verify that glucose, fructose, and galactose are all six-carbon sugars, confirming they are hexoses.
Research the composition of lactose to confirm it is made of glucose and galactose, thus validating it as a disaccharide.
Conclude that all three statements are true based on the confirmations from the previous steps.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of Archaeans: 1) They have cell walls containing peptidoglycan [peptihdo-GLY-can]; 2) They are unicellular; 3) They can be autotrophs.
explainAnswer: Review the characteristics of Archaeans to understand their cellular structure.
Identify that Archaeans do not have peptidoglycan in their cell walls, which makes statement 1 false.
Confirm that Archaeans are unicellular organisms, making statement 2 true.
Recognize that Archaeans can be autotrophs, thus validating statement 3 as true.

text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the Apatosaurus?
choices: It could crack its tail like a whip to ward off would-be attackers
An adult weighed as much as 20 elephants
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of the Apatosaurus based on scientific evidence.
Evaluate each statement provided in the choices against known facts about the Apatosaurus.
Determine which statement does not align with the established understanding of the Apatosaurus' diet and physical traits.
Conclude that the statement 'It was an omnivore' is not true, as Apatosaurus was primarily herbivorous.

text: A diver finds an underwater cave filled with bacteria that seem to feed on volcanic sulfur vents. What type of organisms are these?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of nutrition the bacteria are using to obtain energy.
Recognize that organisms feeding on inorganic compounds, such as sulfur, are classified based on their energy source.
Differentiate between the types of organisms: heterotrophs consume organic material, phototrophs use light, and chemotrophs use chemical compounds.
Conclude that since the bacteria feed on volcanic sulfur, they are chemotrophs.

text: The organ of Corti is directly involved in what human sense?
explainAnswer: Identify the organ of Corti as a structure located in the cochlea of the inner ear.
Recognize that the cochlea is part of the auditory system.
Understand that the organ of Corti contains hair cells that convert sound vibrations into electrical signals.
Conclude that these signals are interpreted by the brain as sound, thus relating the organ of Corti to the sense of hearing.

text: DNA ligase [LYE-gase] is an enzyme that catalyzes which of the following reactions?
explainAnswer: Understand the function of DNA ligase, which is to join DNA strands together.
Recall that phosphodiester bonds are the linkages that connect the sugar and phosphate groups in the DNA backbone.
Eliminate options that involve cutting bonds, as DNA ligase does not cut bonds but rather forms them.
Identify that the correct answer must involve the formation of phosphodiester bonds, which is the primary role of DNA ligase.

text: In human nerves, the nerve impulse or message occurs primarily because of the movement of ions of what two elements across the cell membranes of nerves:
explainAnswer: Recall the basic mechanism of nerve impulse transmission, which involves changes in membrane potential.
Identify the key ions involved in depolarization and repolarization of the nerve cell membrane.
Recognize that sodium ions (Na+) are primarily responsible for depolarization, while potassium ions (K+) are involved in repolarization.
Eliminate the other choices by confirming they do not include both sodium and potassium as the primary ions involved.

text: A tick sucks blood from a cow. Which of the following is this species interaction?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of interaction between the tick and the cow.
Determine if both organisms benefit, if one benefits at the expense of the other, or if they compete for resources.
Recognize that in this case, the tick benefits by feeding on the cow's blood, while the cow is harmed.
Conclude that this interaction is best classified as parasitism.

text: Which of the following types of molecules is not generally composed of a long chain of monomers?
explainAnswer: Identify the general structure of each molecule type listed in the choices.
Recognize that proteins, DNA, and starch are polymers made from long chains of monomers.
Understand that fatty acids are typically not long chains of monomers but rather consist of a hydrocarbon chain with a carboxyl group.
Conclude that fatty acids do not fit the description of being composed of long chains of monomers.

text: Which of the following North American spiders' bite could be fatal to humans?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of each spider listed in the choices.
Research the venom potency and potential health risks associated with each spider's bite.
Determine which spider is known for having a bite that can lead to severe medical complications or fatalities in humans.
Conclude that the Brown recluse is the only spider among the choices that is commonly associated with fatal bites.

text: Which of the following best describes antibodies:
choices: a class of polysaccharides involved in the immune system
a group of proteins made by plasma cells in response to a foreign substance
small bodies of insects that look like ants
a class of genes produced by the immune system to fight disease
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics of antibodies in the immune system.
Eliminate choices that do not relate to proteins or the immune response.
Focus on the role of plasma cells in producing antibodies.
Select the choice that accurately describes antibodies as proteins made in response to foreign substances.

text: You have isolated a pathogen which contains RNA surrounded by a protein coat, but which lacks other cellular organelles. What type of pathogen is it?
explainAnswer: Identify that the pathogen contains RNA, which indicates it is a type of nucleic acid.
Note that it is surrounded by a protein coat, suggesting it has a capsid.
Recognize that the absence of cellular organelles is characteristic of viruses.
Conclude that the combination of RNA and a protein coat without cellular structures defines it as a virus.

text: In vascular plants, what is the name of the transport tissue that primarily carries water to the plant?
explainAnswer: Recall the main types of vascular tissues in plants, which are xylem and phloem.
Identify the function of each type of vascular tissue.
Recognize that xylem is responsible for transporting water and minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant.
Conclude that the transport tissue that primarily carries water is xylem.

text: What scientific term means inflammation of the joints?
explainAnswer: Identify the key term related to joint inflammation.
Recall common medical terms associated with joints.
Recognize that 'arthro' refers to joints and 'itis' refers to inflammation.
Combine the two parts to form the term 'arthritis'.
