text: What is the term for the process by which smooth muscle in the arterioles [ahr-TEER-ee-ohlz] relaxes, resulting in a larger diameter?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of muscle involved in the process, which is smooth muscle.
Understand the context of arterioles and their role in blood flow.
Recognize that the relaxation of smooth muscle leads to an increase in the diameter of the arterioles.
Recall the specific term used to describe the process of blood vessel dilation, which is vasodilation.

text: Which of the following characteristics is NOT true of cannonball jellyfish?
choices: They can make up more than 16% of biomass in shallow inshore areas off the southeastern coast of the United States
One of their main predators is the leatherback sea turtle
They can reproduce both sexually and asexually
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics listed in the choices.
Research each characteristic to determine its accuracy regarding cannonball jellyfish.
Eliminate the characteristics that are true based on your research.
Select the characteristic that is not true as the correct answer.

text: What compartment of the heart pumps blood to the lungs?
explainAnswer: Identify the main compartments of the heart: right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle.
Understand the flow of blood through the heart and its function in pulmonary circulation.
Recognize that the right ventricle is responsible for pumping deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation.

text: Thigmotropism [thig-moh-TROHP-ism] in vines can allow them to wrap around other branches to grow higher. This form of taxis occurs in response to which of the following stimuli?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of thigmotropism, which is a growth response to physical contact.
Consider the options given: Light, Gravity, Touch, Heat.
Determine which option relates to a physical stimulus that causes a plant to respond by wrapping around objects.
Recognize that Touch is the only option that directly corresponds to the definition of thigmotropism.

text: Leprosy is a bacterial disease that results in skin lesions and nerve damage. Which of the following animals is known to be a common host of this disease?
explainAnswer: Recall that leprosy is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium leprae.
Identify the animals listed and their known associations with diseases.
Research which of the listed animals are known to carry or host Mycobacterium leprae.
Determine that armadillos are commonly known to be a host for leprosy.
Select armadillos as the correct answer based on this information.

text: Which of the following is NOT a steroid?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of steroids and their characteristics, such as being lipids with a specific structure including four fused carbon rings.
Examine each option to determine if it fits the definition of a steroid.
Recognize that cholesterol, testosterone, and estradiol are all steroids due to their structural characteristics.
Conclude that triacylglycerols, which are fats composed of glycerol and fatty acids, do not fit the steroid definition.

text: Which of the following was determined in 2007 to be the cause of hundreds of pet deaths because of pet food contamination:
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which is about pet food contamination and its causes.
Recall significant events or findings related to pet food safety around 2007.
Evaluate the choices given and determine which substance was linked to pet deaths during that time.
Confirm that melamine was indeed reported as the contaminant responsible for the pet deaths.

text: What part of the cotton plant produces what is used to make cotton fabric.
explainAnswer: Identify the parts of the cotton plant and their functions.
Understand that cotton fabric is made from the fibers of the cotton plant.
Recognize that the flowers or seed pods are where the cotton fibers are produced.
Eliminate other options that do not produce fibers used for fabric.

text: Which of the following is a feeding structure in arachnids:
explainAnswer: Identify the feeding structures associated with different animal groups.
Recall that arachnids belong to the class Arachnida, which includes spiders and scorpions.
Recognize that chelicerae are specialized mouthparts found in arachnids used for feeding.
Eliminate the other options: dentipalps are found in crustaceans, radula is a feeding structure in mollusks, and proboscis is typically associated with insects.

text: Which of the following is the difference between a viroid [VY-roid] and a virus?
choices: Viroids do not contain a protein coat; viruses do
Viroids only contain RNA; viruses also contain protein
Viroids only contain DNA; viruses also contain protein
Viroids contain DNA; viruses do not
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics of viroids and viruses.
Recall that viroids are simpler than viruses and do not have a protein coat.
Compare the structural components of both viroids and viruses.
Select the statement that accurately reflects the difference in structure regarding the protein coat.

text: Pampas, steppes, and savannas are all different types of:
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of pampas, steppes, and savannas.
Recognize that all three are dominated by grasses rather than trees.
Eliminate the other options (deserts, tropical forests, tropical shrublands) that do not fit this description.
Conclude that the correct category for these ecosystems is grasslands.

text: Which of the following is the most practical method that could be used to isolate proteins for reinjection into mice?
explainAnswer: Identify the goal of isolating proteins for reinjection into mice.
Evaluate each method based on its ability to purify proteins effectively.
Determine that affinity chromatography specifically targets and isolates proteins based on their binding properties.
Conclude that affinity chromatography is the most practical method for this purpose.

text: Humans cannot completely digest plants because we cannot break down their cell walls. Which of the following is an enzyme you would expect to be present in an herbivore?
explainAnswer: Identify the main reason humans cannot digest plants, which is the inability to break down cell walls.
Recognize that herbivores eat plants and need enzymes to digest plant material.
Evaluate the given enzyme options and determine which one is specifically responsible for breaking down cellulose in plant cell walls.
Select cellulase as the enzyme that herbivores would have to digest plant material effectively.

text: Plant cells differ from animal cells in that only plant cells possess:
explainAnswer: Identify the key differences between plant and animal cells.
Recall that plant cells have a rigid structure that provides support.
Recognize that this structure is known as the cell wall.
Eliminate the other options by confirming they are present in both plant and animal cells.

text: List the following five classifications in order from least to most specific: 1) genus, 2) order, 3) phylum [FY-luhm], 4) domain, 5) family.
explainAnswer: Understand the hierarchy of biological classification, which ranges from broad categories to specific ones.
Identify the classifications given: domain, phylum, order, family, and genus.
Rank these classifications from least specific to most specific: domain is the broadest, followed by phylum, then order, family, and finally genus as the most specific.
List the classifications in the correct order: domain (4), phylum (3), order (2), family (5), genus (1).

text: Which of the following is the hormone produced by the human body to control blood sugar and when not produced in sufficient amounts is the cause of some forms of diabetes:
explainAnswer: Identify the function of each hormone listed in the choices.
Recall the role of insulin in regulating blood sugar levels.
Determine which hormone is specifically linked to diabetes when not produced adequately.
Select the hormone that matches the description given in the question.

text: A scientist has fluorescently labelled enzymes of the Calvin cycle. To what organelle does the color localize?
explainAnswer: Identify that the Calvin cycle is a series of biochemical reactions that occur in photosynthetic organisms.
Recall that the Calvin cycle takes place in the chloroplasts of plant cells.
Understand that fluorescently labelled enzymes would localize to the organelle where they function.
Conclude that the color from the fluorescent label would localize to the chloroplast.

text: What term in leaf classification is used to describe leaves consisting of leaflets or lobes radiating from the base?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of leaf structures.
Look for terms that describe the arrangement of leaflets or lobes.
Determine which term specifically refers to leaves that radiate from a central point at the base.
Conclude that the correct term for this type of leaf classification is 'palmate.'

text: Which division of the nervous system contains axons of sensory and motor neurons bundled together as nerves?
explainAnswer: Identify the main divisions of the nervous system: central nervous system (CNS) and peripheral nervous system (PNS).
Understand that the CNS consists of the brain and spinal cord, while the PNS includes all other neural elements.
Recognize that nerves are formed by bundles of axons from sensory and motor neurons.
Conclude that the division of the nervous system containing these bundled axons is the peripheral nervous system.

text: In a plant, what is the term for the region of active growth that contains cells that are actively differentiating?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms related to plant biology.
Recall the structures in plants responsible for growth.
Determine which structure is associated with active cell division and differentiation.
Conclude that the term for this growth region is meristem.

text: What gas essential to human life do plants give off when they photosynthesize?
explainAnswer: Recall the process of photosynthesis in plants.
Identify the primary products of photosynthesis.
Recognize that one of these products is a gas essential for human life.
Conclude that the gas produced is oxygen.

text: What type of plant cells have thin, flexible primary walls and perform most of the metabolic functions of the plant?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of different plant cell types.
Recall that parenchyma cells have thin, flexible primary walls.
Note that parenchyma cells are involved in metabolic functions such as photosynthesis and storage.
Conclude that the type of plant cells described is parenchyma.

text: Plasma is the part of human blood that consists mostly of which of the following?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of human blood, which include red blood cells, white blood cells, plasma, and platelets.
Understand that plasma is the liquid portion of blood that carries cells and proteins.
Recall that plasma is composed of approximately 90% water.
Eliminate the other choices based on their composition and function in blood.
Conclude that the correct answer is water, as it is the primary component of plasma.

text: During the summer months, which of the following plant structures is NOT a sugar sink?
explainAnswer: Understand that a sugar sink is a part of the plant that consumes or stores sugars produced during photosynthesis.
Identify that leaves are primarily involved in photosynthesis and produce sugars rather than consuming them.
Recognize that flowers, roots, and fruits typically use or store sugars, making them sugar sinks.
Conclude that since leaves produce sugars, they are not considered sugar sinks.

text: Consider the cross of two plants, one of which has red flowers and one of which has white flowers. Given that 50% of their offspring have white flowers and 50% have red flowers and assuming complete dominance and independent assortment, identify all of the following three statements that can be concluded from this cross: 1) The red flower trait is dominant to the white flower trait; 2) One of the plants is homozygous for the trait that it possesses; 3) The white- flowered plant is heterozygous for the trait that it possesses.
explainAnswer: Identify the phenotypes of the parent plants: one has red flowers and the other has white flowers.
Recognize that the offspring exhibit a 1:1 ratio of red to white flowers, indicating that one parent must be homozygous and the other heterozygous.
Determine that since 50% of the offspring are white, the white-flowered parent must be homozygous recessive, while the red-flowered parent must be heterozygous.
Conclude that the statement about one plant being homozygous is true based on the offspring ratios and the dominance relationship.

text: In humans, ovulation usually occurs how many days before the start of the next menstrual period:
explainAnswer: Understand the menstrual cycle, which typically lasts about 28 days.
Identify that ovulation usually occurs around the midpoint of the cycle.
Calculate the midpoint by dividing the cycle length by 2, which gives approximately 14 days.
Recognize that ovulation occurs about 14 days before the start of the next menstrual period.

text: Which of the following terms is used to define benthic organisms that live in the spaces between particles of sediment?
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of each term provided in the choices.
Determine which term specifically refers to organisms living in the spaces between sediment particles.
Eliminate the terms that do not match this definition.
Confirm that 'Meiofauna' is the correct term for these organisms.

text: Which of the following statements about flatworms is NOT correct?
choices: Flatworms have no true body cavity and an incomplete digestive system
Flatworms do not have a respiratory system
There are true blood vessels present in the flatworms
The flatworms have a ladder-like nervous system with a distinct head region that includes nerve cells and sensory organs
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of flatworms based on biological knowledge.
Review each statement to determine if it accurately describes flatworm anatomy and physiology.
Recognize that flatworms are acoelomates and lack true blood vessels.
Conclude which statement is incorrect based on the established facts about flatworms.

text: Which of the following is most advantageous to plants that depend on insects for pollination:
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of each option and how they relate to pollination.
Consider the role of pollen in attracting and adhering to insects for effective pollination.
Evaluate which option enhances the likelihood of pollen transferring from one flower to another via insects.
Determine that sticky pollen is the most beneficial trait for plants relying on insect pollinators.

text: Which of the following is NOT a monomer?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a monomer, which is a small molecule that can join together to form larger structures called polymers.
List the given options and categorize them: amino acids and nucleotides are monomers, while glucose is a simple sugar that can also act as a monomer.
Recognize that maltose is a disaccharide, which is formed by the combination of two glucose molecules, thus making it a polymer rather than a monomer.
Conclude that maltose is the only option that is not a monomer.

text: Arginine [AHR-juh-neen] is a positively charged amino acid in water. This amino acid is considered which of the following?
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of arginine, noting that it has a positively charged side chain in aqueous solution.
Recall that amino acids can be classified based on their side chains as acidic, basic, neutral, or amphoteric.
Determine that a positively charged side chain indicates that the amino acid can accept protons, which is characteristic of basic amino acids.
Conclude that since arginine has a basic side chain, it is classified as a basic amino acid.

text: Which of the following is NOT a trait of RNA which has been used to explain why it may have preceded DNA as the first information molecule?
choices: RNA is less stable than DNA
RNA is more stable than DNA
explainAnswer: Identify the traits of RNA mentioned in the question.
Evaluate each trait to determine its validity regarding RNA's characteristics.
Recognize that RNA is generally considered less stable than DNA due to its structure.
Select the statement that contradicts the established understanding of RNA stability, which is that RNA is more stable than DNA.

text: Pheromones are chemicals produced by various species and function primarily in:
explainAnswer: Identify the role of pheromones in biological systems.
Consider the options provided: camouflage, digestion, sweat secretion, and communication.
Recall that pheromones are known to influence behavior and interactions between individuals of the same species.
Eliminate options that do not relate to behavior or interaction.
Select communication as the correct answer based on the role of pheromones.

text: Place the following four steps of mitosis in their proper order: 1) Anaphase; 2) Telophase; 3) Metaphase; 4) Prophase.
explainAnswer: Understand the stages of mitosis: Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, and Telophase.
Identify that Prophase is the first stage where chromosomes condense and the nuclear envelope breaks down.
Recognize that Metaphase follows, where chromosomes align at the cell's equatorial plane.
Note that Anaphase is next, where sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite poles.
Conclude with Telophase, where the chromosomes de-condense and the nuclear envelope re-forms.

text: By name or number, indicate which one or ones of the following biomes that animals with thick fur and large amounts of fat storage would most likely live in: 1) coniferous forest, 2) savannah, 3) rainforest, 4) tundra, and/or 5) temperate forest.
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of animals with thick fur and large amounts of fat storage, which are adaptations for cold environments.
Evaluate each biome listed to determine which ones have cold climates that would require such adaptations.
Coniferous forests are typically found in colder regions, making them suitable for these animals.
The tundra is also a cold biome where animals would need thick fur and fat for insulation and energy storage.
Eliminate the other biomes (savannah, rainforest, temperate forest) as they are warmer and do not require such adaptations.

text: Many antibiotics inhibit bacterial protein synthesis, but not eukaryotic [YOU-care-ee-AW-tic] protein synthesis. Which of the following best explains why?
choices: The antibiotics cut up bacterial mRNA, but not eukaryotic mRNA
Eukaryotes [YOU-care-ee-oats] have enzymes to destroy the antibiotics, but bacteria do not
Eukaryotes can export the antibiotics, preventing them from damaging the cell
The antibiotics affect bacterial but not eukaryotic ribosomes
explainAnswer: Identify the key difference between bacterial and eukaryotic ribosomes.
Understand that antibiotics target specific structures or functions in bacteria.
Evaluate the answer choices based on their relevance to ribosome structure.
Select the choice that correctly states the effect of antibiotics on bacterial ribosomes compared to eukaryotic ribosomes.

text: Neurons have very stereotyped electro-physiological activity that behaves in an "all-or- none" pattern. What is the name of this activity?
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics of neuronal activity described in the question.
Recognize that the term 'all-or-none' refers to a specific type of electrical signal in neurons.
Recall the terminology used in neuroscience to describe this electrical signal.
Conclude that the correct term for this activity is 'action potential'.

text: Which of the following organisms is NOT a habitual biped?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a habitual biped, which refers to organisms that primarily walk on two legs.
Analyze each organism in the choices to determine their primary mode of locomotion.
Kangaroo mice and ostriches are known for their bipedal movement, while gibbons can walk on two legs but also use their arms for swinging.
Recognize that proboscis monkeys primarily move on all fours and are not considered habitual bipeds.
Conclude that the correct answer is the proboscis monkey, as it does not primarily walk on two legs.

text: The human retina is made up of tiny, light-sensitive cells. Which of these cells enable us to distinguish colors?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of light-sensitive cells in the human retina, which are rods and cones.
Understand the primary function of rods, which is to detect light intensity and not color.
Recognize that cones are responsible for color vision.
Conclude that cones enable us to distinguish colors.

text: Which of the following interactions is the best example of commensalism?
choices: A cleaner fish eats parasites from a larger fish
An oak tree blocks the sunlight of a nearby sapling
A wasp lays its eggs inside of a caterpillar
A dung beetle eats the feces of a buffalo
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of commensalism, which is a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed.
Review each choice to determine which interaction fits this definition.
In the first choice, the cleaner fish benefits while the larger fish is helped, indicating mutualism.
In the second choice, the oak tree harms the sapling by blocking sunlight, which is not commensalism.
In the third choice, the wasp harms the caterpillar, indicating parasitism.
In the fourth choice, the dung beetle benefits from eating the buffalo's feces, while the buffalo is unaffected, fitting the definition of commensalism.

text: The exchange of gases between blood and the tissue occurs normally in:
explainAnswer: Identify the function of each type of blood vessel: arteries carry blood away from the heart, veins carry blood back to the heart, venules are small veins, and arterioles are small arteries.
Recognize that gas exchange occurs at the site where blood is closest to tissues, which is primarily in the smallest blood vessels.
Determine that capillaries are the smallest blood vessels and are specifically designed for the exchange of gases, nutrients, and waste between blood and tissues.
Conclude that since capillaries are the primary site for gas exchange, they are the correct answer.

text: Colony collapse disorder is a phenomenon associated with what animals?
explainAnswer: Recall the definition of colony collapse disorder and its symptoms.
Identify the types of animals that live in colonies.
Consider which of these animals are known to experience significant population declines.
Recognize that honey bees are a key species affected by this phenomenon.

text: What are the five most common chemical elements of living biological matter?
answer: OXYGEN, CARBON, HYDROGEN, NITROGEN, AND PHOSPHORUS
explainAnswer: Recall the basic building blocks of life and the elements that are essential for biological processes.
Identify the most abundant elements found in living organisms.
List the elements that are crucial for the structure of proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids.
Confirm that the five elements are oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, and phosphorus.
Remember that these elements are often referred to as the 'CHNOPS' elements.

text: What is the name for the process by which plants absorb light from the Sun and convert it to chemical energy?
explainAnswer: Identify the process by which plants use sunlight.
Recall that this process involves converting light energy into chemical energy.
Recognize that the term commonly used to describe this process is 'photosynthesis'.

text: A population crash is most likely when which of the following occurs?
explainAnswer: Understand the concept of carrying capacity, which is the maximum population size that an environment can sustain.
Recognize that when a population overshoots carrying capacity, it exceeds the resources available, leading to a rapid decline in population.
Evaluate the other choices to see if they relate to a population crash; unlimited resources and a slowed growth rate do not directly cause a crash.
Conclude that the most likely scenario for a population crash is when the population overshoots carrying capacity.

text: Silviculture is a branch of agricultural science that is concerned with the development and care of what?
explainAnswer: Identify the field of study mentioned in the question, which is silviculture.
Understand the definition of silviculture as it relates to agricultural science.
Recognize that silviculture focuses on the cultivation and management of trees and forests.
Conclude that the correct answer pertains to the development and care of forests.

text: Which of the following is NOT a type of sampling used by field scientists?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of sampling commonly used in field studies.
Review the definitions of each sampling method listed in the choices.
Determine which of the listed methods is not recognized as a standard sampling technique.
Conclude that Null sampling is not a type of sampling used by field scientists.

text: What will occur to an animal cell if it is placed in a hypotonic environment?
explainAnswer: Understand that a hypotonic environment has a lower concentration of solutes compared to the inside of the cell.
Recognize that water will move into the cell through osmosis to balance the solute concentrations.
Determine that as water enters the cell, it will swell due to the increased volume.
Conclude that if too much water enters, the cell membrane may not withstand the pressure and will burst, leading to the cell exploding.

text: What is the name for the outermost germ layer?
explainAnswer: Recall the three primary germ layers in embryonic development: ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm.
Identify which layer is the outermost among these three.
Recognize that the outermost layer is called the ectoderm.

text: In the traditional 5 Kingdom classification of organisms, four of the 5 Kingdoms are Animalia, Plantae, Fungi, and Protista. What is the fifth?
explainAnswer: Recall the traditional 5 Kingdom classification system used in biology.
Identify the four known kingdoms: Animalia, Plantae, Fungi, and Protista.
Recognize that the fifth kingdom is the one that includes prokaryotic organisms.
Conclude that the fifth kingdom is Monera, which consists of bacteria and archaea.

text: Which of the following animals best exhibits aposematic [ap-oh-seh-MAT-ik] coloration as a defense mechanism?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of aposematic coloration, which is a warning coloration used by animals to signal that they are toxic or unpalatable.
Evaluate each animal in the choices to see if they have bright colors that indicate danger or toxicity.
Consider the bee, which is known for its bright yellow and black coloration and its ability to sting, signaling a warning to potential predators.
Compare the other animals: leopards and zebras have camouflage or disruptive coloration, while chameleons can change color but do not typically exhibit aposematic coloration.
Conclude that the bee is the best example of aposematic coloration among the given options.

text: Mendel did most of his original experimentation using this type of plant:
explainAnswer: Recall the key experiments conducted by Gregor Mendel in genetics.
Identify the plant species that Mendel used for his experiments.
Recognize that Mendel's work primarily focused on the inheritance patterns of traits in this plant.
Conclude that the plant he used is commonly known as the pea plant.

text: Heartburn is generally caused by stomach acids flowing into which other organ?
explainAnswer: Identify the symptoms and causes of heartburn.
Understand the role of stomach acids in digestion.
Determine which organ is affected when stomach acids flow back.
Conclude that the esophagus is the organ that experiences this reflux.

text: What stage of cellular respiration ends with the production of pyruvate (read as: py-RUH-vayt)?
explainAnswer: Identify the stages of cellular respiration: glycolysis, Krebs cycle, and electron transport chain.
Recall that glycolysis is the first stage of cellular respiration.
Understand that glycolysis converts glucose into pyruvate.
Conclude that the stage of cellular respiration that ends with the production of pyruvate is glycolysis.

text: What is the name of a small, circular piece of bacterial DNA that contains only a few genes?
explainAnswer: Recall that bacteria often have a main circular DNA molecule called chromosomal DNA.
Identify that bacteria can also have smaller, additional pieces of DNA that are separate from the chromosomal DNA.
Recognize that these smaller DNA pieces usually contain a few genes and are often involved in functions like antibiotic resistance.
Conclude that the term used to describe these small, circular pieces of bacterial DNA is plasmid.

text: In humans, red-green color blindness is caused by a recessive sex-linked trait on the X chromosome. If a man and a woman produce a color blind son, assuming no spontaneous mutation, which of the following must be true?
choices: Both parents carry the allele for color blindness
The mother carries the allele for color blindness
Neither parent carries the allele for color blindness
explainAnswer: Recognize that color blindness is a recessive trait linked to the X chromosome.
Understand that a son inherits his X chromosome from his mother and his Y chromosome from his father.
Since the son is color blind, he must have received the color blindness allele from his mother.
Conclude that the mother must carry at least one allele for color blindness to pass it on to her son.

text: Encephalitis is an inflammation of what organ?
explainAnswer: Identify the term 'encephalitis' and break it down into its components: 'encephal' refers to the brain.
Recall that 'itis' is a suffix commonly used in medical terminology to indicate inflammation.
Combine the meanings of the components to conclude that encephalitis refers to inflammation of the brain.

text: What is the term used to describe the embryonic leaf in a seed?
explainAnswer: Identify the parts of a seed and their functions.
Recall the terminology associated with seed development.
Recognize that the embryonic leaf is a specific structure within the seed.
Conclude that the term used for the embryonic leaf is cotyledon.

text: The ocean’s distinct smell comes from dimethyl sulfide (DMS), which is released upon the death of what ocean organism?
explainAnswer: Identify the organisms listed in the choices and their roles in the ocean ecosystem.
Recall that dimethyl sulfide (DMS) is a compound associated with the decomposition of organic matter.
Recognize that phytoplankton are primary producers in the ocean and are abundant in marine environments.
Consider that when phytoplankton die, they release DMS, contributing to the ocean's distinct smell.
Select phytoplankton as the correct answer based on the association with DMS release.

text: Which of the following is NOT a method by which speciation is known to occur?
choices: A group of similar animals moves to a new landmass with no natural predators
A busy highway is built through a forest
A predator randomly selects animals from a prey population to consume
Chromosome ploidy changes during plant reproduction
explainAnswer: Identify the methods of speciation, such as geographic isolation, reproductive isolation, and polyploidy.
Analyze each option to determine if it describes a mechanism that leads to speciation.
Recognize that a predator selecting prey does not create reproductive isolation or lead to the formation of new species.
Conclude that the correct answer is the option that does not describe a speciation method.

text: What is the term for the point on a stem at which a leaf is attached?
explainAnswer: Recall the basic structure of a plant stem.
Identify the specific area where leaves emerge from the stem.
Recognize that this point is referred to as a node in botanical terminology.

text: What general type of human blood vessel returns blood to the heart?
explainAnswer: Identify the main types of blood vessels in the human circulatory system: arteries, veins, and capillaries.
Understand the function of each type of blood vessel: arteries carry blood away from the heart, veins return blood to the heart, and capillaries facilitate exchange.
Focus on the specific function of veins in relation to blood flow direction.
Conclude that the general type of blood vessel that returns blood to the heart is a vein.

text: A gardener is trying to graft two fruit trees together. Which type of hormone should she use to form callus tissue to connect the plants?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of hormones in plant growth and development.
Understand that auxins are responsible for cell elongation and the formation of callus tissue.
Recall that callus tissue is essential for grafting as it helps in the healing and connection of plant tissues.
Conclude that auxin is the appropriate hormone to promote callus formation in grafting.

text: What type of biological structures have no apparent function, but resemble structures that are found in the evolutionary history of an organism?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question, such as 'biological structures' and 'evolutionary history'.
Recall the definition of structures that may not serve a current function but are remnants of ancestral forms.
Connect the concept of evolutionary biology to find the term that describes these structures.
Conclude that the answer is 'vestigial structures' based on the definitions and connections made.

text: By words or numbers, name all of the following 3 physical or chemical changes that will typically denature a protein: 1) large changes in pH; 2) rapid cooling to 4ºC; 3) heating to over 45ºC
explainAnswer: Identify the conditions that typically denature proteins, focusing on pH and temperature changes.
Recall that extreme pH levels can disrupt hydrogen bonds and ionic interactions in proteins.
Recognize that heating proteins to temperatures above 45ºC can cause them to unfold and lose their functional structure.
Determine that rapid cooling to 4ºC does not typically denature proteins, but rather stabilizes them.
Conclude that the correct answers are large changes in pH and heating to over 45ºC.

text: Over the course of their lives, plants will build significant carbon-based biomass without reducing the mass of the soil they are growing in. From what molecule does the carbon for this biomass come?
explainAnswer: Identify that plants undergo photosynthesis to create biomass.
Recognize that during photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
Understand that carbon dioxide is a key source of carbon for building organic molecules in plants.
Conclude that the carbon for plant biomass comes from carbon dioxide.

text: Which of the following is least likely to be found in a hot desert climate?
choices: A plant with broad flat leaves
A plant with thick fleshy leaves
A plant with thin needle-like leaves
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of a hot desert climate, such as high temperatures and low water availability.
Consider the adaptations plants need to survive in such an environment, like reduced leaf surface area to minimize water loss.
Evaluate each choice based on these adaptations, focusing on how broad flat leaves would increase water loss.
Conclude that a plant with broad flat leaves is least likely to survive in a hot desert climate.

text: Into which of the following does a typical fern spore most directly develop:
explainAnswer: Understand that ferns reproduce via a life cycle that includes both sporophyte and gametophyte stages.
Recognize that spores are produced by the sporophyte and are the means of reproduction.
Identify that when a fern spore germinates, it develops into a gametophyte.
Eliminate the other options (sporophyte, egg cell, sperm cell) as they do not directly follow spore development.

text: Which of the following is the most distinguishing characteristic of all vertebrates adapted to life on land from amphibians:
choices: presence of a coelom (read as: sil-OHM)
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics that differentiate vertebrates adapted to land from amphibians.
Consider the reproductive strategies of both groups, focusing on egg development.
Recognize that amphibians typically have a larval stage and do not produce amniotic eggs.
Determine that the presence of amniotic eggs is a significant adaptation for life on land, allowing for development without water.
Conclude that the production of amniotic eggs is the most distinguishing characteristic.

text: Which group of fungi has never been observed reproducing sexually?
explainAnswer: Identify the different groups of fungi based on their reproductive methods.
Understand that fungi are classified into groups such as Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes, and Deuteromycetes.
Recognize that the group known as Deuteromycetes, or imperfect fungi, has only been observed reproducing asexually.
Conclude that the correct answer is the group of fungi that has never been observed reproducing sexually, which is the IMPERFECT fungi.

text: Which of the following does NOT characterize dicotyledon plants?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of dicotyledon plants, which typically include net-like leaf venation, tap roots, and flowers with petals in multiples of four or five.
Review the options provided to see which characteristic does not align with those of dicotyledons.
Recognize that parallel veins on leaves are a characteristic of monocotyledons, not dicotyledons.
Conclude that the option 'Parallel veins on leaf' does not characterize dicotyledon plants.

text: Name all of the following 3 choices that are common functions of feathers on birds: thermal insulation; sexual selection; flight
explainAnswer: Identify the three functions listed: thermal insulation, sexual selection, and flight.
Research or recall the roles of feathers in birds.
Determine if each function is commonly associated with feathers.
Conclude that all three functions are indeed common uses of feathers in birds.

text: In a mating between a color blind human male and a normal vision female with a color blind father, what is the percentage chance a son would be color blind?
explainAnswer: Identify the genetic traits involved: color blindness is an X-linked recessive trait.
Determine the genotypes of the parents: the color blind male is X^cY and the normal vision female, having a color blind father, is X^NX^c.
Set up a Punnett square to cross the male's genotype with the female's genotype.
Analyze the offspring possibilities: sons will inherit the Y chromosome from the father and one X chromosome from the mother.
Calculate the percentage of sons that will be color blind based on the Punnett square results, which shows a 50% chance.

text: What is the term for the flexible tissue that holds bones together?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of connective tissues in the body.
Recall the function of ligaments in the skeletal system.
Differentiate between ligaments and other connective tissues like tendons.
Conclude that the term for the flexible tissue that holds bones together is ligament.

text: What structures, composed of flexible tissue, connect two or more bones together at joints?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question, such as 'structures', 'flexible tissue', 'connect', 'bones', and 'joints'.
Recall the types of connective tissues in the body and their functions related to joints.
Determine which connective tissue specifically connects bones to each other at joints.
Conclude that the correct answer is ligaments, as they are the structures that fulfill this role.

text: What are the two major organs that degrade hormones?
explainAnswer: Recall the primary functions of the liver and kidneys in the body.
Identify the role of these organs in metabolism and excretion.
Consider which organs are involved in breaking down and eliminating hormones.
Conclude that the liver and kidneys are the two major organs responsible for degrading hormones.

text: Which of the following best describes a coelacanth (read as: SEE-la-canth):
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of a coelacanth, noting its ancient lineage and unique features.
Research the term 'living fossil' and understand that it refers to species that have remained relatively unchanged over millions of years.
Compare the coelacanth to the other choices provided to determine which description aligns best with its biological classification and history.
Conclude that 'living fossil fish' accurately describes the coelacanth due to its long evolutionary history and current existence.

text: If an animal has 42 chromosomes in its normal, non-gamete or somatic cells, what term would be given to the gametes that have 21 chromosomes:
explainAnswer: Identify that somatic cells contain the full set of chromosomes, which is 42 in this case.
Recognize that gametes are reproductive cells that contain half the number of chromosomes compared to somatic cells.
Calculate half of 42 chromosomes, which is 21.
Understand that the term used for cells with half the number of chromosomes is 'haploid'.
Choose 'haploid' from the provided options.

text: What is the average internal Celsius temperature of the human body?
explainAnswer: Recall that the average internal body temperature is a well-established fact.
Identify the standard temperature measurement used for human body temperature, which is in Celsius.
Recognize that the average internal body temperature is approximately 37 degrees Celsius.

text: Which of the following is the most common cause of deaths in American women between the ages of 20 and 40?
explainAnswer: Identify the age range specified in the question, which is 20 to 40 years old.
Consider the common health issues and causes of death that affect women in this age group.
Evaluate the options provided: AIDS, breast cancer, colon cancer, and heart attacks.
Research or recall statistics regarding the leading causes of death for women in this demographic.
Determine that breast cancer is the most prevalent cause of death among the listed options for women aged 20 to 40.

text: What are the names of the four chambers of the human heart?
answer: LEFT VENTRICLE, RIGHT VENTRICLE, LEFT ATRIUM, RIGHT ATRIUM
explainAnswer: Recall the basic anatomy of the human heart.
Identify the two upper chambers, which are the atria.
Identify the two lower chambers, which are the ventricles.
List the chambers in pairs: left atrium, right atrium, left ventricle, right ventricle.

text: What functional group is characteristic of ketones and aldehydes?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of functional groups in organic chemistry.
Recognize that ketones and aldehydes are both types of carbonyl compounds.
Define the carbonyl functional group as a carbon atom double-bonded to an oxygen atom.
Differentiate between ketones (which have carbonyl groups flanked by carbon atoms) and aldehydes (which have a carbonyl group at the end of a carbon chain).
Conclude that the characteristic functional group for both ketones and aldehydes is the carbonyl group.

text: If a cell is placed in a hypotonic solution, what effect will osmosis have on the cell?
choices: It will become turgid or lyse
explainAnswer: Understand that a hypotonic solution has a lower concentration of solutes compared to the inside of the cell.
Recognize that water will move into the cell through osmosis to balance the solute concentrations.
Determine that as water enters, the cell will swell and may become turgid.
Conclude that if too much water enters, the cell may eventually lyse or burst.

text: Place the following three events in order from earliest to latest in the process of generating protein from a DNA sequence in eukaryotes: 1) Translocation of mRNA to the cytoplasm; 2) Transcription; 3) Translation.
explainAnswer: Identify the process of protein synthesis, which involves transcription, translation, and mRNA processing.
Recognize that transcription is the first step where DNA is converted into mRNA.
Understand that after transcription, the mRNA must be processed and then translocated to the cytoplasm.
Finally, translation occurs in the cytoplasm where the mRNA is used to synthesize proteins.

text: Which of the following is the principle difference between the two types of active transport?
choices: Primary active transport involves an electrochemical gradient, while secondary active transport involves chemical energy
Primary active transport involves chemical energy, while secondary active transport involves an electrochemical gradient
Primary active transport involves moving ions into a cell, while secondary active transport involves moving ions out of a cell
Primary active transport involves moving ions out of a cell, while secondary active transport involves moving ions into a cell
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of primary and secondary active transport.
Understand that primary active transport directly uses chemical energy, typically from ATP.
Recognize that secondary active transport relies on the electrochemical gradient created by primary active transport.
Compare the roles of chemical energy and electrochemical gradients in both types of transport.
Select the statement that accurately describes the difference based on your understanding.

text: If an order of plant has floral parts usually arranged in multiples of 4 or 5, it would most likely have:
choices: vascular bundles arranged in a ring and a taproot
diffuse or fibrous root system and 2 cotyledons
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of the plant order described, focusing on floral part arrangements.
Recall that plants with floral parts in multiples of 4 or 5 typically belong to the dicot group.
Understand that dicots usually have vascular bundles arranged in a ring and often exhibit a taproot system.
Eliminate the other choices based on their characteristics that do not align with dicots.

text: Which of the following is an ecosystem service provided by the ocean? W) Providing safe passage to mariners X) Restricting access to deep-ocean species Y) Sanitizing water in the hydrologic cycle Z) Absorbing heat from the sun's light
answer: Z) ABSORBING HEAT FROM THE SUN'S LIGHT
explainAnswer: Identify the options provided and categorize them based on their relevance to ecosystem services.
Recall the definition of ecosystem services and what functions they serve in the environment.
Evaluate each option to determine if it describes a natural process that benefits the ecosystem.
Recognize that absorbing heat from the sun's light is a crucial function of the ocean that helps regulate climate.
Select the option that correctly describes an ecosystem service, which is Z) Absorbing heat from the sun's light.

text: What is the nitrogenous [ny-TROJ-uh-nuhs] base found in RNA that is NOT present in DNA?
explainAnswer: Recall the basic components of nucleic acids, which include nitrogenous bases, sugars, and phosphate groups.
Identify the four nitrogenous bases found in DNA: adenine, thymine, cytosine, and guanine.
List the four nitrogenous bases found in RNA: adenine, uracil, cytosine, and guanine.
Compare the two lists to determine which base is present in RNA but not in DNA.
Conclude that uracil is the nitrogenous base found in RNA that is not present in DNA.

text: Rickets is caused by a deficiency of what vitamin?
explainAnswer: Identify the symptoms and effects of rickets, which include weak or soft bones.
Research the nutritional deficiencies that lead to these symptoms.
Determine which vitamins are essential for bone health and development.
Conclude that a deficiency in vitamin D specifically leads to rickets.

text: What organ of the human body is primarily responsible for eliminating abnormal red blood cells from the circulation and then recycling iron to the bone marrow ?
explainAnswer: Identify the organs involved in blood cell regulation and recycling.
Recall the functions of the spleen in the immune system and blood filtration.
Determine which organ is specifically known for eliminating abnormal red blood cells.
Confirm that the spleen also recycles iron for use in the bone marrow.

text: The act of girdling a tree would most likely be done by which of the following?
explainAnswer: Identify the meaning of girdling, which involves removing a strip of bark from a tree.
Consider which of the listed animals are known to consume or damage tree bark.
Evaluate the feeding habits of porcupines, woodpeckers, tent caterpillars, and starlings.
Determine that porcupines are the only ones that typically girdle trees by eating the bark.

text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of heterokonts?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of heterokonts from the provided choices.
Recall that heterokonts are a diverse group that includes both freshwater and saltwater species.
Determine which statement does not accurately describe the heterokonts based on your knowledge.
Select the statement 'Most species prefer salt water' as it is not a defining characteristic.

text: Most bacteria undergo a form of asexual reproduction in which the cells divide into two. What is the term for this type of reproduction?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of reproduction being described in the question.
Recall the common methods of asexual reproduction in bacteria.
Recognize that the process of dividing into two is a specific term used in biology.
Conclude that the term for this type of reproduction is fission.

text: Where is intercellular fluid normally found?
answer: OUTSIDE OF CELLS (ACCEPT: IN BETWEEN CELLS OR IN THE
explainAnswer: Understand that intercellular fluid refers to the fluid found between cells.
Recognize that this fluid is part of the extracellular fluid compartment.
Identify that intercellular fluid is not located inside the cells themselves.
Conclude that intercellular fluid is normally found outside of cells or in the spaces between them.

text: In humans, chemical digestion of protein does NOT occur in which of the following areas?
explainAnswer: Identify the locations in the human digestive system where protein digestion occurs.
Recall that protein digestion begins in the stomach with the action of pepsin.
Recognize that the small intestine continues protein digestion with enzymes from the pancreas.
Understand that the brush border is involved in the final stages of digestion but not in initial protein breakdown.
Conclude that the mouth does not have the enzymes necessary for protein digestion.

text: Which type of cell becomes cancerous in people who develop leukemia?
explainAnswer: Understand that leukemia is a type of cancer that affects the blood and bone marrow.
Identify that the primary cells involved in the immune response are white blood cells.
Recognize that in leukemia, these white blood cells become abnormal and multiply uncontrollably.
Conclude that the type of cell that becomes cancerous in leukemia is the white blood cell.

text: Which of following correctly pairs a monomer with one of its corresponding polymers?
explainAnswer: Identify the monomers and their corresponding polymers from the choices given.
Recall that glucose is a monomer that can polymerize to form cellulose.
Eliminate the other options by verifying that they do not correctly match monomers with their polymers.
Confirm that glucose is indeed the correct monomer for the polymer cellulose.

text: The most common form of color blindness results in the difficulty of distinguishing what two primary colors?
answer: RED AND GREEN (ACCEPT IN ANY ORDER)
explainAnswer: Recall the primary colors in the RGB color model, which are red, green, and blue.
Identify the most common type of color blindness, which is red-green color blindness.
Understand that this condition primarily affects the ability to distinguish between red and green colors.
Conclude that the two primary colors that are difficult to distinguish are red and green.

text: What is the largest terrestrial biome, characterized by large populations of coniferous [koh-NIH-fur-us] trees?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of each biome listed in the choices.
Recognize that coniferous trees are a key feature of certain biomes.
Determine which biome is known for having large populations of coniferous trees.
Select the option that matches this description, which is the Taiga.

text: By name or number, identify all of the following four choices that are examples of birth defects: 1) spina bifida, 2) hypospadias (read as: hy-poh-SPAY-dee- ahs), 3) Tay-Sachs, 4) phenylketonuria (read as: fee-nil-kee-tohn-UHR-ee-ah).
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a birth defect as a condition present at birth that affects the structure or function of the body.
Review each choice to determine if it is a condition that fits the definition of a birth defect.
Confirm that spina bifida, hypospadias, Tay-Sachs, and phenylketonuria are all recognized as birth defects.
List all identified birth defects as the final answer.

text: Name the two living monotremes.
explainAnswer: Recall that monotremes are a group of egg-laying mammals.
Identify the two known species of monotremes that are still alive today.
Recognize that the duck-billed platypus is one of the species.
Identify the echidna as the second living monotreme.

text: Which of the following is an example of organisms found living next to hydrothermal vents.
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of organisms that thrive in extreme environments.
Recognize that hydrothermal vents are extreme environments with high temperatures and pressure.
Recall that extremophiles are organisms specifically adapted to live in such harsh conditions.
Eliminate the other options that do not refer to organisms adapted to extreme environments.

text: What organelle with attached ribosomes is most directly responsible for the translation of proteins destined to be transported out of the cell?
explainAnswer: Identify the organelles involved in protein synthesis and transport.
Recognize that ribosomes are responsible for translating mRNA into proteins.
Determine which organelle has ribosomes attached to its surface.
Conclude that the organelle with attached ribosomes responsible for transporting proteins is the endoplasmic reticulum.

text: Identify all of the following four organelles that are thought to have evolved from endosymbionts [endo-SIM-by-awnts]: 1) Mitochondrion [my-tow-KON-dree-on]; 2) Chloroplast; 3) Nucleus; 4) Lysosome [LYE-soh-sohm].
explainAnswer: Recall the endosymbiotic theory, which suggests that certain organelles originated from free-living prokaryotes that were engulfed by ancestral eukaryotic cells.
Identify which of the listed organelles are involved in energy production and photosynthesis, as these are typically associated with endosymbiotic origins.
Recognize that mitochondria are responsible for cellular respiration and chloroplasts are involved in photosynthesis, both of which support the endosymbiotic theory.
Eliminate the nucleus and lysosome from consideration, as the nucleus is a defining feature of eukaryotic cells and lysosomes are derived from the Golgi apparatus, not endosymbionts.

text: What is a tool used to identify organisms that consists of a series of paired statements or questions that describes alternative possible characteristics of the organism and the presence or absence of certain visible structures or characteristics?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of the tool described in the question.
Recognize that it involves a series of paired statements or questions.
Understand that it is used for identifying organisms based on visible traits.
Recall the specific term that fits this description, which is a dichotomous key.

text: Which of the following is a TRUE statement about fructose and glucose?
choices: They have the same molecular structure
They are both disaccharides (read as: dy-SAH-keh-ryds)
explainAnswer: Identify the molecular formulas of fructose and glucose, which are both C6H12O6.
Recognize that although they share the same molecular formula, they are structural isomers.
Understand that structural isomers have different arrangements of atoms, leading to different molecular structures.
Eliminate the options that state they have the same molecular structure or that they are disaccharides, as both are monosaccharides.
Conclude that the true statement is that they have different molecular structures.

text: By number, identify all of the following five characteristics which are TRUE of lancelets: 1) they are filter feeders; 2) they have an open circulatory system; 3) their blood is colorless; 4) they have no heart; 5) they have a tail.
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of lancelets based on biological knowledge.
Evaluate each characteristic to determine its truthfulness regarding lancelets.
List the characteristics that are true: filter feeders, colorless blood, no heart, and having a tail.
Exclude the characteristic about having an open circulatory system as it is false.

text: Differentiation of cells during plant development is MOST commonly associated with:
choices: allowing cells to recognize other cells
explainAnswer: Identify the key concept of differentiation in plant development.
Understand that differentiation refers to the process where cells become specialized for specific functions.
Evaluate the provided choices to see which one aligns with the definition of differentiation.
Select the choice that describes the process of cells maturing into specialized cells.

text: All of the following cells undergo mitosis EXCEPT:
explainAnswer: Identify the process of mitosis and its purpose in cell division.
Review the characteristics of each cell type listed in the choices.
Determine which of the cells typically do not undergo mitosis after reaching maturity.
Recognize that red blood cells lose their nucleus and do not divide, unlike the other cell types.

text: On the Galapagos Islands, Darwin discovered 13 species of finches that possess specialized beaks for unique environments. Which of the following evolutionary principles is exemplified by this phenomenon?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of adaptive radiation, which involves the diversification of a group of organisms into forms filling different ecological niches.
Recognize that Darwin's finches evolved distinct beak shapes to adapt to various food sources on the Galapagos Islands.

Eliminate other choices by understanding that convergent evolution refers to unrelated species developing similar traits, parallel evolution involves related species evolving similarly, and coevolution is about two species influencing each other's evolution.
Conclude that the phenomenon of Darwin's finches is best explained by adaptive radiation due to their rapid diversification in response to environmental challenges.

text: Which of the following best characterizes the material that is presented by antigen-presenting cells to T cells?
explainAnswer: Understand that antigen-presenting cells (APCs) process and present antigens to T cells.
Recall that the primary form of antigens presented by APCs to T cells is through Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) molecules.
Recognize that MHC molecules typically present short peptide fragments derived from proteins.
Eliminate the other choices (protein domains, RNA sequences, DNA sequences) as they do not accurately describe the form of antigens presented to T cells.

text: Which of the following anatomical structures do sharks NOT possess:
explainAnswer: Identify the anatomical structures listed in the choices.
Research the anatomy of sharks to determine which structures they possess.
Compare the listed structures with known shark anatomy to find the one that is absent.
Conclude that sharks do not have gill covers or opercula.

text: What is the first amino acid encoded by all eukaryotic mRNAs [yoo-KAR-ee-oh-tik]?
explainAnswer: Understand that eukaryotic mRNAs are translated into proteins starting from a specific amino acid.
Recall that the genetic code specifies that the start codon is AUG.
Recognize that AUG codes for the amino acid methionine.
Conclude that methionine is the first amino acid in all eukaryotic mRNAs.

text: What structure is created during plant cell mitosis that is NOT present in the splitting of animal cells?
explainAnswer: Understand the differences between plant and animal cell mitosis.
Identify the key structures involved in cytokinesis for both types of cells.
Recognize that animal cells form a cleavage furrow, while plant cells form a cell plate.
Conclude that the structure created during plant cell mitosis that is not present in animal cells is the cell plate.

text: Which of the following can be found in eukaryotes [YOU-care-ee-oats] , but not in prokaryotes [PRO-care-ee-oats] ?
explainAnswer: Identify the key differences between eukaryotes and prokaryotes.
Recall that eukaryotes have membrane-bound organelles while prokaryotes do not.
List the organelles mentioned in the choices and determine which are membrane-bound.
Recognize that mitochondria are membrane-bound organelles found only in eukaryotic cells.
Conclude that mitochondria is the correct answer as it is not found in prokaryotes.

text: What is the name of the triplet of bases in the mRNA that codes for a specific amino acid?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of mRNA in protein synthesis.
Recall that mRNA is made up of nucleotide bases.
Understand that a sequence of three bases corresponds to a specific amino acid.
Recognize that this sequence of three bases is called a codon.

text: Which of the following magnifications is most appropriate for viewing bacteria through a light microscope?
explainAnswer: Understand that bacteria are typically in the range of 0.5 to 5 micrometers in size.
Recognize that to view objects of this size clearly, a higher magnification is necessary.
Consider the options given and determine which magnification would allow for sufficient detail to observe bacteria.
Identify that 500 times magnification is suitable for viewing small organisms like bacteria, while lower magnifications would not provide enough detail.

text: If you were a pirate in the 15 th century, you might very well suffer from scurvy. In order to prevent the disease, which of the following should you consume?
explainAnswer: Identify the disease and its cause, which is a deficiency of vitamin C.
Recall that scurvy is historically linked to sailors and pirates who lacked fresh fruits and vegetables.
Consider which of the given options is a rich source of vitamin C.
Determine that oranges are known for their high vitamin C content, making them the best choice to prevent scurvy.

text: The beta-galactosidase enzyme aids in lactose digestion by separating lactose into what two monosaccharide molecules?
explainAnswer: Identify the substrate that the enzyme acts upon, which is lactose.
Understand that lactose is a disaccharide made up of two monosaccharides.
Recall the two monosaccharides that compose lactose, which are galactose and glucose.
Conclude that the enzyme beta-galactosidase separates lactose into galactose and glucose.

text: Thyroid disease is typically thought of as:
explainAnswer: Identify the primary function of the thyroid gland, which is to regulate metabolism.
Consider the role of thyroid hormones in controlling energy use and metabolic processes in the body.
Eliminate options that do not directly relate to metabolism, such as blood disorders and digestive system disorders.
Confirm that thyroid disease primarily affects metabolic functions, supporting the choice of metabolic disease.

text: Identify all of the following three characteristics that are possessed by both plants and animals: 1) Nuclear envelope; 2) Mitochondria [my-tow-KON-dree-ah] ; 3) Chloroplasts [KLOR-oh-plasts] .
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics listed in the question.
Determine which of the characteristics are found in both plants and animals.
Confirm that both plants and animals have a nuclear envelope and mitochondria.
Note that chloroplasts are only found in plants, not animals.
Conclude that the correct characteristics possessed by both are the nuclear envelope and mitochondria.

text: Which of the following relative dating principles relies on fossils for dating?
explainAnswer: Identify the principles of relative dating mentioned in the question.
Understand that faunal succession refers to the use of fossilized remains to determine the relative ages of rock layers.
Eliminate the other options by recognizing that they do not specifically rely on fossils for dating.
Conclude that faunal succession is the correct answer as it directly involves fossils.

text: A phage can incorporate its DNA into the bacterial chromosome in the lysogenic cycle of infection. What is the term for the viral DNA that is embedded in the host DNA?
explainAnswer: Understand the concept of the lysogenic cycle in viral infections.
Identify the process by which viral DNA integrates into the host's genetic material.
Recall the specific terminology used to describe viral DNA that is incorporated into the host DNA.
Conclude that the term for this integrated viral DNA is 'provirus'.

text: While most complexes in the cell are made of proteins, ribosomes are mostly composed of protein and what other macromolecule?
explainAnswer: Identify the primary components of ribosomes.
Recall that ribosomes are involved in protein synthesis.
Recognize that ribosomes consist of both proteins and another type of macromolecule.
Determine that the other macromolecule present in ribosomes is nucleic acids, specifically rRNA.

text: What part of the brain coordinates the movements of the body and is thought to be the location of "muscle memory?"
explainAnswer: Identify the main functions of different parts of the brain.
Recall which part of the brain is responsible for coordination and balance.
Consider the concept of 'muscle memory' and where it is processed in the brain.
Conclude that the part of the brain that fits both functions is the cerebellum.

text: Cell membranes are described as fluid mosaic models consisting of proteins embedded in a bilayer of phospholipids. Which of the following components of a plant cell do NOT contain two of these bilayers?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of a plant cell listed in the question.
Recall the structure of each component and whether they have a double bilayer membrane.
Determine that chloroplasts and mitochondria have two bilayers, while the endoplasmic reticulum has only one.
Conclude that the endoplasmic reticulum is the correct answer as it does not contain two bilayers.

text: Kate is constructing a cladogram [KLAD-oh-gram] that includes angiosperms, conifers, ferns, and mosses. Which of the following is most likely to be an ancestral trait of this cladogram?
explainAnswer: Identify the traits listed in the choices and determine which are more primitive or ancestral.
Consider the evolutionary history of the groups: mosses are non-vascular, ferns are vascular but do not have seeds, and angiosperms and conifers both have seeds.
Recognize that stems are present in all the groups listed, making them a more likely ancestral trait.
Eliminate the other traits: flowers and seeds are derived traits specific to certain groups, while vasculature is not present in mosses.

text: Which of the following is an autoimmune disease:
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of an autoimmune disease, which is a condition where the immune system attacks the body's own cells.
Review the list of choices provided: Lupus, spina bifida, scabies, yellow fever.
Determine which of these conditions is characterized by the immune system attacking its own tissues.
Recognize that Lupus is known to be an autoimmune disease, while the others are not.
Conclude that the correct answer is Lupus.

text: What is the term for the junction where neurons communicate with each other?
explainAnswer: Identify the key concept related to neuron communication.
Recall the biological terminology associated with neurons.
Match the concept with the correct term used in neuroscience.
Confirm that the term is commonly used to describe the junction between neurons.

text: Which of the following is a gas which presents a serious risk for cancer to thousands of Americans?
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of each gas listed in the choices.
Research the health risks associated with each gas, focusing on their potential carcinogenic effects.
Determine which gas is known to be a significant health hazard related to cancer.
Conclude that Radon is the gas that presents a serious cancer risk.

text: The medulla [meh-DULL-ah], pons, and midbrain collectively form what structure of the brain?
explainAnswer: Identify the three components mentioned: medulla, pons, and midbrain.
Recall the functions and locations of these components within the brain.
Recognize that these three parts are collectively known for their role in connecting the brain to the spinal cord.
Conclude that the structure formed by these components is called the brainstem.

text: Glucose is the main source of energy for most animals. What form of energy is glucose?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which is about energy sources in animals.
Recall that glucose is a type of sugar and is involved in metabolic processes.
Understand that energy stored in glucose is released during cellular respiration.
Recognize that the energy stored in glucose is in the form of chemical bonds.
Conclude that the correct answer is 'chemical' energy.

text: What is the name of the equation that biologists use to calculate the frequencies of alleles in a population?
explainAnswer: Recall that the Hardy-Weinberg principle relates to genetic variation in a population.
Identify that the equation is used to predict allele frequencies under certain conditions.
Recognize that the equation is named after the two scientists, Hardy and Weinberg, who formulated it.
Conclude that the answer to the question is the name of the equation, which is 'Hardy-Weinberg'.

text: Which of the following is a common excitatory neurotransmitter in mammals:
explainAnswer: Identify the role of neurotransmitters in the nervous system.
Review the list of given options and categorize them based on their functions.
Recall that excitatory neurotransmitters stimulate the nervous system and promote the transmission of signals.
Recognize that acetylcholine is known to be an excitatory neurotransmitter in mammals.
Eliminate the other options as they do not primarily function as neurotransmitters.

text: Flower color is determined by two alleles, R for red and w for white. Flower color exhibits incomplete dominance, meaning a flower with genotype Rw will be pink in color. If a pink flower and a white flower are crossed, what percentage of the offspring will become red?
explainAnswer: Identify the genotypes of the parent flowers: the pink flower is Rw and the white flower is ww.
Set up a Punnett square to determine the possible genotypes of the offspring from the cross Rw x ww.
Fill in the Punnett square to find the resulting genotypes: Rw, Rw, ww, ww.
Analyze the offspring genotypes: there are no R alleles in the offspring, so none can be red.
Conclude that 0% of the offspring will be red.

text: If you were told you were anemic and had to increase your dietary iron uptake, which of the following foods would provide the most iron:
explainAnswer: Identify the iron content in each food option.
Research the dietary iron levels of green beans, spinach, beef spleen, and broiled chicken thighs.
Compare the iron content values to determine which food has the highest amount of iron.
Select the food item with the highest iron content as the answer.

text: What is the name of the highly specialized oxygen-transport molecule in the blood that carbon monoxide binds with much more tightly than oxygen does?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of oxygen-transport molecules in the blood.
Recall the primary molecule responsible for transporting oxygen in the bloodstream.
Consider the interaction of carbon monoxide with this molecule.

text: According to the principle of complementary base pairing, if you have DNA that consists of 15% thymine, what is the percentage of cytosine in the molecule?
answer: 35% (Note that thymine does not pair with cytosine; It pairs with guanine.)
